title: Distributed Systems Engineer 5 - Data Platform Poland
locations: Warsaw, Poland
descriptionHtml:
At Netflix, our mission is to entertain the world. Together, we are writing the next episode - pushing the boundaries of storytelling, global fandom and making the unimaginable a reality. We are a dream team obsessed with the uncomfortable excitement of discovering what happens when you merge creativity, intuition and cutting-edge technology. Come be a part of what’s next.

We provide centralized data platforms and tools for various business functions at Netflix, enabling teams to utilize data to make critical, data-driven decisions. We focus on making it easy for our business partners to work with data efficiently, securely, and responsibly. We aspire to set the industry standard in building a world-class data infrastructure, supporting Netflix’s vision to be the most popular and widely accessible destination for global internet entertainment.


As the Data Platform charter grows, we are expanding our presence to Poland to further increase our impact. We are seeking Distributed Systems Engineers to help evolve and innovate our Product and Infrastructure. We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive team that brings new perspectives as we address the next set of challenges.


Team Spotlights


Analytics Platform and Experience Team

Owns the architecture and foundational systems of Netflix's Analytics Platform, a growing domain with an expanding charter as the platform scales to support critical initiatives like Live and Ads. The team currently owns automated Spark migration tooling and TableDiff. As the charter grows, the team will soon take ownership of the Trino engine and lead additional high-impact platform initiatives. This offers an excellent opportunity to shape foundational data infrastructure and deliver direct, high-leverage impact across Netflix.


Data Movement Team

The Data Movement Connector EcoSystem at Netflix is a growing domain with an expanding charter to own high-leverage business-critical connectors across Netflix. The team currently offers Frameworks, Libraries, and Control Planes and supports a large set of streaming/incremental and batch/snapshot-based connectors. This offering evolves the next step is full ownership of the Mantis ecosystem. We believe having the Poland team build and own a set of connectors to move and integrate data across different business domains would be the fastest way to unlock business values. This offers an excellent opportunity to learn the technology stack and deliver direct, relevant impact across the organization.


Online Data Stores Team

This team takes end-to-end ownership of key parts of Netflix’s Online Data Stores (ODS) platform, the databases and data abstractions behind Netflix’s online services. Ownership covers everything from design and development to day-to-day operations and on-call. The team’s charter spans three core areas:

1. Relational databases (PostgreSQL on AWS Aurora)
Ownership of Netflix’s managed relational database platform, used by product teams across Netflix such as Games, Ads and Commerce. The goal is to turn it from “a database you get” into a true platform abstraction: one-click provisioning and lifecycle management, proactive capacity management and auto-scaling, a smarter data plane (connection pooling, read/write routing, query guardrails), fleet-wide observability with GenAI-assisted diagnosis, and safe, paved-path access to data for both developers and AI agents.

2. Document databases
Ownership of Netflix’s document data store domain. This includes running and supporting today’s document storage solution and its customers, and defining and building the next Netflix paved path for document databases, from engine evaluation and build-vs-buy decisions to production rollout and customer migrations.

3. Core data platform infrastructure
Ownership of critical foundational services such as ZooKeeper, ensuring their reliability, scalability and continued evolution, along with the self-service capabilities that let Netflix engineers provision, operate and reason about their datastores independently.

The mission is to boost Netflix engineers’ productivity and innovation through a robust, efficient and secure data platform, while working closely with partner teams across Data Platform in the US and Poland.


Experimentation Platform Team

This team owns the data infrastructure that makes A/B testing work at Netflix. Specifically, they build and maintain the systems that store and govern the record of who was in which experiment, across hundreds of concurrent tests running across streaming, ads, growth, and device platforms. They also own the semantic layer that ties every experiment metric at Netflix back to that allocation data, and the pipelines that keep the whole thing fresh and reliable. As the team matures, the scope grows to include self-service tooling for the teams running experiments and support for AI-driven monitoring and analysis workflows.

This could be a great opportunity for you if you enjoy:

  • Solving business needs at scale by applying your software engineering and analytical problem-solving skills
  • Designing and building robust, scalable, and highly available distributed infrastructure
  • Leading cross-functional initiatives and collaborating with engineers, product managers, and technical program managers across teams
  • Sharing experiences with open source communities and contributing to Netflix OSS

About you:

  • 7 or more years of experience designing and building complex, scalable distributed systems and/or infrastructure
  • Proficiency in Java (preferred), Python, Scala, Kotlin or C# with a solid understanding of multi-threading and memory management
  • Demonstrated experience developing and maintaining impactful systems
  • You have developed your skills through a variety of educational or professional experiences in computer science, engineering, or a related field
  • Experience with any of the following is additive: Spark/Flink/Trino/Druid platform

A few more things about us:
As a team, we come from many different backgrounds and countries. Our fields of education range from the humanities to engineering to computer science, and we strive to give people the opportunity to take on different roles, should they choose to. We believe that this diversity and adaptability have helped us build an inclusive and empathetic environment, and we look forward to adding your perspective.

Our culture is unique, and we tend to live by our values, so it’s worth learning more about Netflix here. 

Inclusion is a Netflix value and we strive to host a meaningful interview experience for all candidates. If you want an accommodation/adjustment for a disability or any other reason during the hiring process, please send a request to your recruiting partner.

We are an equal-opportunity employer and celebrate diversity, recognizing that diversity builds stronger teams. We approach diversity and inclusion seriously and thoughtfully. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, ancestry, national origin, caste, sex, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity or expression, age, disability, medical condition, pregnancy, genetic makeup, marital status, or military service.

Job is open for no less than 7 days and will be removed when the position is filled.

title: Analytics Engineer 5 - Infrastructure Efficiency & Productivity
locations: Remote, United States
descriptionHtml:
At Netflix, our mission is to entertain the world. Together, we are writing the next episode - pushing the boundaries of storytelling, global fandom and making the unimaginable a reality. We are a dream team obsessed with the uncomfortable excitement of discovering what happens when you merge creativity, intuition and cutting-edge technology. Come be a part of what’s next.

Everything that we build to delight our members relies on our extensive technical infrastructure, which spans from services we rent from AWS to our custom-built content delivery network, Open Connect. As that infrastructure grows, so does investment in AI tooling, and understanding how efficiently we use both is central to Netflix's investment decisions.

As a Senior Analytics Engineer on Platform Data Science & Engineering, you will own how Netflix understands the efficiency of its cloud and AI infrastructure. You will join a data org of Analytics Engineers, Data Engineers, Visualization Engineers, and Data Scientists who partner with engineering teams and leadership to define the metrics, build the datasets, and deliver the insights that the company relies on to spend wisely. Your work will be the trusted source of truth that engineers and executives use to make decisions about a multi-billion-dollar infrastructure footprint.

This is a broad, high-visibility role with a lot of white space. You'll have the opportunity to develop metrics from scratch, build the logic and pipelines behind them, tell the story through dashboards and analyses, and turn all of it into recommendations that change how teams invest. You'll also help pioneer one of the most salient problems in the industry: quantifying the productivity impact of an increasingly AI- and agent-augmented workforce, where there is no textbook answer and real room to set the standard.

The ideal candidate will excel in metric research and development, self-sufficient analytics engineering, and data storytelling, and will share a passion for continuously improving how we use data to enhance Netflix's infrastructure.

To learn more about our team, read here.

In this role, you will:

  • Define and own the core metrics for how Netflix understands infrastructure cost, usage, and efficiency across its compute, storage, streaming, and machine learning platforms, and expand that coverage as the footprint grows.

  • Help pioneer new ways to measure the productivity impact of AI tooling and autonomous agents, shaping frameworks that leadership across the company will use to guide investment.

  • Increase the speed and quality with which the company understands and acts on its efficiency, turning what is often slow, manual analysis into trusted, reusable insight.

  • Surface and size new efficiency opportunities, translating patterns in cost and usage data into recommendations that lead directly to meaningful savings.

  • Tell the story with data: build the dashboards, reports, and narratives that make efficiency legible to audiences from individual engineers to senior executives, partnering with our visualization engineers on the surfaces that serve them.

  • Partner with Data Engineers on the pipelines upstream of your metrics, and with Data Scientists on the forecasting and reliability work that connects to yours.

You are:

  • Experienced in metric research and development in a technical domain: you build metric frameworks (not just one-off metrics) at multiple granularities that ladder up to a coherent whole, and you set targets people trust.

  • Self-sufficient across the full analytics loop: data exploration, cleaning, light pipeline building, business logic, and dashboards. Fluent in Python and SQL.

  • At home in messy, changing data, with the judgment to know when a number is right and when it needs a second look.

  • An exceptional communicator with both technical and non-technical audiences, experienced at telling stories with data and influencing decisions at all levels of the business.

  • A strong product thinker with good product sense: you get at what your partners actually need and build solutions that satisfy it.

  • Comfortable with ambiguity, and you thrive with minimal oversight and process.

  • Thoughtful about using AI in your own craft, using coding and analytics agents well, and evaluating what they produce rather than taking it on faith.

  • Experienced in measuring cost, efficiency, or system performance in a cloud or streaming context (a plus), or motivated to go deep in that domain.

title: Business Security Partner (L5), Consumer & Content
locations: Remote, United States
descriptionHtml:
At Netflix, our mission is to entertain the world. Together, we are writing the next episode - pushing the boundaries of storytelling, global fandom and making the unimaginable a reality. We are a dream team obsessed with the uncomfortable excitement of discovering what happens when you merge creativity, intuition and cutting-edge technology. Come be a part of what’s next.

The Team

Netflix’s Business Security Partner (BSP) team is a team of senior security advisors organized around business proximity rather than technical domains. Each BSP partner owns relationships with a defined portfolio of business units, builds long-term relationships with BU leadership, and serves as the security export who understands those businesses well enough to advise on decisions before they are made. We sit in business reviews, participate in architecture conversations, and build the kind of trust with stakeholders that makes security a resource rather than a requirement. 

Across all of our relationships, the goal is the same: every major business decision at Netflix should have access to clear, usable security risk context; not a compliance output buried in a document, but actionable guidance from a partner who understands both the risk and the business. 

About the Role

This role covers two distinct and fast-moving areas within Netflix.  BSP aligns coverage based on need; BSPs also often rotate business units on occasion. You may cover other areas during your time at Netflix.

On the Customer Service side, you will be the primary security partner for a global support organization that is deploying AI capabilities across its consumer-facing operations. You will advise on the security risk of new technologies as they launch, help the organization assess and manage risk for systems that handle significant consumer data volumes, and maintain the overall security posture for a high-scale, globally operating support environment 

For Content Generation, you will partner with teams that are building the next generation of GenAI / GenMedia production pipelines; prosperity models, open-source tools, and third-party inference providers running on CPU compute infrastructure to generate visual context for Netflix productions. Your work will span third-party AI tool evaluations, compute infrastructure security, training data governance, and security control decisions for AI-assisted content workflows. You will partner with multiple cross-functional teams to drive remediation of identified risks. The content these systems touch is pre-release Netflix IP, and the pace of change is high.

This role also carries M&A responsibilities. BSPs at Netflix are expected to support technical security due diligence for acquisitions and subsidiaries. 

What You Will Work On:

  • Own the security partnership for Customer Service and Creative Technology, building stakeholder relationships, learning how these businesses operate, and translating that context into opinionated security guidance.

  • Lead security risk assessments and treatment strategies with cross-functional teams as they launch new capabilities and tools.

  • Evaluate and advise on the security posture of GenAI/GenMedia - third-party tool evaluations, open-source model assessments, compute infrastructure security, and training data governance.

  • Maintain and evolve the Business Risk Profile for each business unit, prioritizing and driving remediation of the risks that matter most.

  • Support M&A technical security due diligence for acquisitions and subsidiaries. 

  • Develop reporting and metrics that communicate risk posture and business security initiatives to SPA leadership and business unit stakeholders.

Desired Background:

  • Experience with securing GenAI systems, customer-facing deployments, and/or content generation / ML pipelines. You understand what makes AI systems distinct from traditional software.

  • Broad security domain knowledge across application security, cloud security, identity and access management, and data governance. You are comfortable operating across all of them and know when to go deep versus when to synthesize. 

  • Strong stakeholder partnership instincts. You build trust with the business by demonstrating that you understand their context, not just their security posture. You know how to translate a technical finding into a business decision, and back to the Security department for support. 

  • Experience advising on security for consumer-facing systems, customer data environments, or high-scale operational technology.

  • Comfort with ambiguity and novel technology environments. You have a framework for reasoning under uncertainty and for making recommendations when the answer isn't fully known.

  • M&A or technical due diligence experience is a plus and not required.

title: Solution Architect - Talent Technology Engineering
locations: Los Gatos, California, United States of America
Los Angeles, California, United States of America
descriptionHtml:
At Netflix, our mission is to entertain the world. Together, we are writing the next episode - pushing the boundaries of storytelling, global fandom and making the unimaginable a reality. We are a dream team obsessed with the uncomfortable excitement of discovering what happens when you merge creativity, intuition and cutting-edge technology. Come be a part of what’s next.


This role is a horizontal architect position for HR Technology. The architect is accountable for designing and governing the foundational HR systems and integrations that HR, Talent teams rely on, across both third‑party (3P) platform. You are responsible for the North Star architecture of 3rd party systems across multiple HR domains and vendors. 


What You’ll Do


1. Architect the HR Tech Ecosystem


North Star & Strategy

  • Define and maintain the target architecture for HR technology across domains 

  • Develop a multi‑year (≈2+ years) architecture roadmap describing how HR systems, integrations, and data models evolve to support business strategy (e.g., growth, new markets, workforce models).


3P + 1P Boundary Setting

  • Determine what capabilities sit in 3P platforms versus 1P services.

  • Decide when to leverage vendor capabilities versus building differentiated 1P experiences.

  • Assess when to consolidate, sunset, or introduce vendors.

  • Establish guardrails for configuration vs customization vs 1P extensions within HR platforms.


Standardization & Paved Roads

  • Establish and own standard patterns for:

    • HR data models (e.g. positions, organizations, compensation, locations).

    • Integrations (APIs, events, batch, and file-based, where necessary).

    • Identity, entitlements, and access control across HR systems.

  • Deliver “out‑of‑the‑box” solutions and reusable templates to minimize one‑off integrations and fragile implementations.


Foundational Systems

  • Lead the architecture of foundational HR systems and services that serve as horizontal sources of truth (e.g., worker master, job catalog, HR events).

  • Ensure these systems meet requirements for completeness, correctness, timeliness, and auditability to support HR and downstream Finance/Compliance needs.

2. Data Architecture (Horizontal Across Domains)


Data Ownership & Lineage

  • Define golden sources for HR entities and how data flows into analytics, Finance, Security, and other consumers.

  • Ensure HR data is traceable, auditable, and explainable from original source to reporting and downstream usage.


Non‑Functional Requirements Embedded

  • Embed security, privacy, and regulatory requirements directly into the architecture, including:

    • Regional data residency and cross‑border data transfer considerations.

    • Role‑based access controls and least‑privilege principles.

    • Employee privacy expectations and internal policies.

  • Partner with Security, Privacy, and Legal to convert these requirements into repeatable technical patterns rather than ad‑hoc process overlays.


3. Decision-Making, Stakeholder Management & Influence

  • Engage with Talent and cross functional  partners to understand processes, pain points, and risk areas 

  • Translate business outcomes into solution architectures that are sustainable, maintainable, and aligned with long‑term strategy, not just limited by immediate tool configuration options.


Influence 

  • Provide architectural direction to engineering teams building 1P services and integrations.

  • Review solution designs and identify approaches that conflict with the target architecture.

  • Enable vertical/domain teams to focus on business needs by ensuring the horizontal foundations are robust and well‑defined.

  • Represent the HR architecture to 3P vendors and partners.

  • Evaluate and, where necessary, challenge vendor proposals that increase complexity, create lock‑in, or duplicate existing 1P capabilities without clear benefit.


Making Trade‑Offs

  • Make explicit, documented decisions on:

    • Short‑term HR needs versus long‑term ecosystem health and simplification.

    • Level of customization versus maintainability, scalability, and upgradeability.

  • Document decisions and rationale and be prepared to revisit them when new evidence emerges.


4. Execution & Ownership

  • Identify opportunities to rationalize redundant tools, platforms, and integrations.

  • Propose and lead decommissioning efforts for low‑value, high‑cost, or overlapping components.

  • Champion an architectural approach that reduces complexity, improves reliability, and lowers total cost of ownership across the HR technology landscape.

Minimum Qualifications

  • 8–12+ years in enterprise engineering/architecture roles, with significant time as a Solutions / HR Tech / ERP architect or equivalent.

  • Hands-on experience architecting ecosystems with multiple 3P HR systems and custom 1P services.

  • Deep understanding of at least one major HCM or HR suite (Workday, SAP SuccessFactors, Oracle HCM, etc.), including integrations and extension patterns.

  • Understanding of Modern integration patterns and data modeling for people/HR domains, and security, privacy, and compliance expectations around employee data.

  • Demonstrated ability to operate as a horizontal architect serving multiple teams.

  • Influence and challenge senior stakeholders (HR, Eng, vendors) with clear, data-driven arguments.

  • Make non-obvious architectural trade-offs and live with the consequences.

Members can play, pause and resume watching, as much as they want, anytime, anywhere, and can change their plans at any time.

Possessing full visibility across the Content slate (both locally and globally), the MPSR team plays a pivotal role in forward planning and campaign prioritization. This team also ensures that local initiatives are seamlessly connected to global priorities and resources and serves as a strategic representative of our internal marketing teams with external creative partners and studios in order to maximize promotional opportunities for their projects worldwide.

The Opportunity

The Manager, Marketing Planning and Studio Relations - India will be responsible for ensuring the seamless execution of marketing campaigns for licensed titles. This role is the connective tissue between Netflix’s internal functions and external studio partners, transforming complex logistical and rights challenges into streamlined, high-impact marketing opportunities.

This role is based in Mumbai, and reports to the Senior Manager, Marketing Planning & Studio Relations based in India.  

Key Responsibilities:
 

Studio Relations:

  • Develop and manage complex relationships with local and global studio partners. Act as a trusted advisor to unlock promotional opportunities while navigating licensing constraints and legal requirements.

  • Educate external partners on Netflix’s marketing standards and operational excellence to ensure high-quality, timely asset delivery.

  • Utilize data and reporting tools to track operational performance, spot trends, and establish "best-in-class" practices for licensed content marketing.

  • Experience in optimizing complex workflows and building scalable marketing operations.

  • Strong organizational and project management skills, with exceptional attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple priorities simultaneously.

descriptionHtml:
At Netflix, our mission is to entertain the world. Together, we are writing the next episode - pushing the boundaries of storytelling, global fandom and making the unimaginable a reality. We are a dream team obsessed with the uncomfortable excitement of discovering what happens when you merge creativity, intuition and cutting-edge technology. Come be a part of what’s next.

Our Experiences team puts fans at the center of their favorite stories, in real life, through permanent entertainment venues, Netflix House, and touring attractions around the world. Netflix Houses are our permanent, always-on, constantly refreshable entertainment venues, where guests can step into their favorite stories. We want these experiences, along with merchandise offerings, to help promote love for our titles so they become part of the zeitgeist for longer periods of time and drive long-term value for Netflix.

Netflix is seeking a Manager, Experiences Retail Store Operations to lead store operations for Netflix's Direct-to-Consumer Retail, with a focus on Netflix House. This role owns store operations end-to-end: from shaping strategy with leadership, to owning the technology and tools that power the stores, to working directly with hourly Retail Crew on the floor. Reporting to the Head of Netflix Experiences Retail, this person will build the processes, systems, and standards for a new and growing retail concept, while making sure day-to-day execution is consistent, efficient, and drives revenue across locations.

The ideal candidate is comfortable working at every level, equally at home presenting a plan to senior leadership and solving a problem on the sales floor mid-shift. They can take a general goal and turn it into a clear, practical process that the Retail Crew can actually follow, and they use data to check that it's working rather than relying on instinct alone. This is a hands-on, build-it-yourself role for someone who wants to help define how a new kind of retail experience runs, including the technology behind it, not just maintain an existing system.

RESPONSIBILITIES

Strategy, Operating Model & Process

  • Define and evolve the store operations strategy for Netflix House and other physical retail touchpoints.

  • Design and maintain the operating model (processes, standards, and SOPs) covering daily store routines, inventory management, fan service, loss prevention, and general store administration.

  • Identify operational gaps through direct floor engagement, Crew feedback, and data analysis, and close them with practical, field-ready solutions.

  • Build, own, and track the efficacy of the loss prevention strategy.

  • Spend periodic time on-site with Retail Crew to understand real operational friction firsthand, building credibility as a partner who solves problems.

Retail Technology & Systems Ownership

  • Own the retail technology stack across venues, including point-of-sale (e.g., Shopify), RFID, inventory management, and other in-store systems and tools.

  • Lead the evaluation, selection, implementation, and ongoing optimization of retail technology to keep Netflix's stores at the forefront of the industry.

  • Partner with IT/Engineering and outside vendors to scope, test, and roll out new systems, managing transitions from planning through go-live.

Performance & Financial Insights

  • Define and monitor key store operations KPIs (inventory accuracy, shrink, sell-through, labor efficiency, guest experience) across venues.

  • Partner with Central Ops and Store Managers to optimize Retail Crew scheduling and hours, ensuring venues are appropriately staffed without overspending on labor.

  • Partner with Finance on store budgets and expense tracking; build reporting that supports leadership decision-making and surface opportunities to improve revenue, conversion, and efficiency.

Cross-Functional Partnership & Communication

  • Act as the main link between HQ strategy and what actually happens on the floor, partnering with Visual Merchandising, Merchandising, Marketing, Finance, and Tech.

  • Partner with Central Ops to ensure a unified approach from Central to onsite teams.

  • Translate cross-functional initiatives (product launches, brand activations, system changes) into clear, store-ready execution plans.

  • Own communications to venue teams, ensuring Crew stay informed without being overwhelmed.

  • Collaborate with our partner vendors and agencies to ensure work is completed on time and on budget according to our agreements.

New Venue Openings & Expansion

  • Lead operational planning and execution for new venue openings, including opening plans, timelines, staffing strategies, training schedules, and readiness checklists.

  • Travel regularly to new and existing venues to support openings, training, and operational assessments.

  • Partner with Design, Construction, Visual Merchandising, IT, and Finance to ensure venues open on time, on budget, and to brand standard.

QUALIFICATIONS

  • 10+ years of retail operations experience, spanning both strategic/HQ-level work and hands-on field or store-level execution.

  • Direct, hands-on experience with retail technology systems: POS platforms (e.g., Shopify), RFID, and inventory management systems, including leading system implementations or major technology transitions.

  • Demonstrated ability to build operational structure in ambiguous, still-forming environments.

  • Data-driven mindset with experience building KPI frameworks, dashboards, and financial/operational reporting.

  • Experience writing and implementing scalable SOPs.

  • Comfortable and credible operating at every level: presenting to senior leadership and working directly alongside hourly Crew.

  • Experience leading new store/venue openings.

  • Willingness to travel regularly to Retail touchpoints.

We celebrate diversity of identities, ideas, backgrounds, and experiences. We believe our best work stems from fostering safety & trust and enabling each of us to be our authentic selves. We selflessly use our unique strengths to support one another and help each other grow.

We have a distributed team with teammates across the US. While some of us are in person, the team is committed to ensuring remote work is a collaborative and productive experience for everyone, regardless of where you commit code.

The Role
This role will have the opportunity to enable a new generation of Netflix experiences by expanding the capabilities of our TV platform. This candidate should be skilled in designing performance-focused UI architectures to support numerous use cases, scale across 100+ engineers, efficiently manage resources, and enable new technology integrations. We’re looking for candidates who balance developer experience and ergonomics with performance, memory, and scalability. This candidate is comfortable applying systems thinking to application architecture and is actively engaged in the industry trends and technologies that support scalable software. This candidate thrives on diving into the inner workings of technologies to understand how they operate and improve their performance, memory, and interfaces.

You
Our team members excel when they are curious, growth-oriented, and collaborative. We take a customer-centric approach to our work, so listening, learning, and adapting are essential. We assume good intent and consistently seek to improve ourselves and our solutions. There are no absolutes, and we must remain flexible to meet the needs of our customers and the business, so “strong opinions loosely held” is a valued attribute within the team.
If this resonates with you, we’d love to talk!

descriptionHtml:

It's an amazing time to join the Netflix team in APAC as we continue to transform entertainment and bring our region’s stories to audiences around the world.

This role sits at the intersection of Netflix's ads story, a diverse set of APAC businesses and markets, and the people inside Netflix — and will be responsible for connecting those dots.

The Team:

Communications at Netflix represents a seasoned group of professionals shaping and telling the story of Netflix as the global leader in streaming entertainment. The work of this team is critical in illustrating the company’s success and reinforcing our reputation in a fast-changing, complex and competitive global landscape. We tell compelling stories about our Netflix titles, brand and local initiatives, working closely with advertising, partnerships, content, policy, publicity, production, and other functions to infuse these stories with their efforts.

Role Overview:

We are seeking a Manager to lead our advertising and partnerships communications in APAC and oversee internal communications across the region.

This role will serve as the regional communications lead for Netflix's advertising business across APAC, connecting our global advertising communications strategy with the needs and opportunities of our local markets. They will partner closely with regional Ads leaders and cross-functional teams, identify stories and opportunities that can travel across the region, and equip local communications teams to tell compelling stories about Netflix's advertising business in their markets.

They should have a strong understanding of the advertising ecosystem and how to leverage communications channels all across APAC, especially Korea, Japan, Australia, and China. Proficiency in Mandarin and English is an advantage, and candidates with a proven track record of new media and social-first storytelling will be preferred.

In addition, the role will lead our internal communications activity across the region — helping APAC staff understand global and regional priorities, feel connected to leadership with regular programs and events, and stay inspired by creative internal campaigns.

The ideal candidate will be a strategic thinker, a strong communicator, and a relationship builder, who can be a trusted partner and adviser to teams across multiple disciplines. This role will create and manage communications strategies, including pitches, announcements, and executive comms both internally and externally (closely partnering with our Regional Leadership Team).  

As Manager, Advertising, Partnerships & Internal Communications - Pan APAC, you will:

  • Craft press narratives and leverage regional storytelling opportunities to shape perceptions across APAC around our ads business and capabilities

  • Be the regional touchpoint for advertising communications — working with local comms and advertising teams to shape story angles and translate business strategy into communications strategy

  • Serve as a trusted communications partner to APAC Ads leaders and cross-functional teams across Sales, Marketing, Measurement, Product and other functions, bringing communications counsel and an informed regional point of view to business priorities

  • Support communications for Netflix's growing Export Ads business, partnering closely with the Singapore-based business team to build the narrative and communications strategy for Mainland China and other export markets

  • Develop and nurture business media relationships, with a deep understanding of the regional press landscape and targeted pitching strategies

  • Be the connective tissue with global advertising comms — ensuring best practice across the region and identifying relevant global opportunities for local teams

  • Touchpoint for our partnership announcements across the region — working closely with the Partnerships team and third party suppliers on a range of bundles and deals.

  • Draft communications plans, announcements, briefing materials, and messaging documents

  • Leveraging locally-led brand partnerships, consumer products, and live experiences to highlight the creativity and innovation within APAC

  • Lead internal communications across APAC — helping employees understand regional and global priorities, strengthening connection with leadership, and developing creative programs that build context and connection across our geographically diverse teams

  • Raise the team's collective capability by applying and sharing AI-driven approaches to reputation monitoring, pitching, drafting, and workflow efficiency

This role is based in Singapore, and reports to the Director, Communications - Pan-APAC.

The candidate must:

  • Have 10+ years of experience in advertising and/or corporate communications

  • Have established working media relationships at trade, entertainment, consumer, and business outlets, along with a keen interest in non-traditional and emerging media channels

  • Clear and concise communication style; strong written and verbal skills that can effectively convey complex ideas

  • Strong ability to work cross-functionally, collaborate with a range of teams across the business to deliver shared impact, and clearly communicate broader business priorities to the wider team

  • Comfort translating technical or product-driven concepts (e.g., ad tech, agentic AI tools) into clear external narratives, partnering effectively with product and technology communications counterparts

descriptionHtml:

EMEA is a growing hub within our broader Data & Insights org, and we are looking for a stunning Senior Data Scientist based in Amsterdam to join our growing Studio Production DSE team. In this role, you will partner with Product Management and cross-functional product teams, Finance & Strategy, and Content Operations & Innovation leadership to scale and innovate content creation workflows. Through thoughtful metric research and causal inference modeling, you will have the opportunity to directly influence decision-making around how we produce and innovate on global content production - helping Creatives bring their best vision to life on screen.

As a Senior Data Scientist in this space, you will:

  • Be the second Applied Inference Data Scientist in Media Science Data Science & Engineering, helping shape how the discipline shows up and drives impact in Studio Production

  • Be a strategic thought partner for Content & Business Product PMs, Content Operations & Innovation leaders and teams, Finance & Strategy, and AI Innovation & Strategy DSE – scoping ambiguous, greenfield questions and proposing data science approaches where no playbook exists

About you:

  • Advanced degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Physics, Economics, or related quantitative field

  • 5+ years of relevant experience with a variety of causal inference methods, including quasi-experimental designs and managing complexities around smaller sample sizes

  • Strong statistical knowledge and intuition, utilized in observational causal analysis and applied machine learning settings, with demonstrated business impact

  • An expert in SQL and Python

  • Proven track record wrangling data, performing exploratory data analysis, designing metrics and tests, building causal inference solutions, and articulating data stories to deliver meaningful business impact

  • Strong verbal and written communicator who can develop and deepen effective relationships with a wide variety of stakeholders and communicate technical concepts clearly and concisely to less technical audiences

  • A self-starter with a learning mindset who is exceptionally curious – eagerly diving into new spaces and bringing informed ideas to the table

  • Comfortable operating in ambiguity and a fast-paced environment; able to take ownership and thrive with minimal oversight and process

  • Thrilled about innovating in the Content Production domain via novel experimental techniques and comfortable taking (smart) risks in your work

  • Extensive experience within the EMEA region, adept at working across different cultures on a globally-distributed team, collaborating with fellow team members and partners to ideate on and deliver impactful research

  • Netflix culture resonates with you

  • Plus: Experience creating data products and dashboards such as Tableau

  • Plus: Designing and analyzing A/B tests

You will have the opportunity to impact the business in a meaningful way, working alongside smart people who love to solve hard problems, and who not only expect but also foster high performance. descriptionHtml:

About the Compute group:

Netflix’s Compute group owns our internet-scale cloud footprint. We constantly innovate to increase fleet-wide agility, efficiency, and reliability of this infrastructure. We build, operate, and maintain Compute services so that Netflix developers can rely on foundational building blocks that enable a “set it and forget it” approach to achieving scalability and cost efficiency. We are responsible for one of the largest Cloud Compute footprints built on AWS, and constantly seeking to push boundaries through innovation to delight hundreds of millions of Netflix users daily.


About the Role:

We are seeking an experienced staff engineer to drive the Node Runtime team’s charter, guide engineering work for the team, and break new ground with hands-on innovation on the hardest technical challenges. You will be part of the team of engineers with a mission to drive innovation in effective, reliable computing at Netflix, and to bring that innovation back to the OSS world. This team tackles some of the largest cloud compute challenges in the industry.  The team owns the Kubernetes data plane software and the container runtime, and we make sure the environment on every Kubernetes node is set up for Netflix Cloud applications to run reliably and with minimal effort. The team partners with many other teams within Netflix to ensure we stay ahead of the business's needs and enable other teams to innovate on top of our platform.


You will be amongst the stunning set of engineers who tackle some of the largest Cloud Compute challenges in the industry. We are moving quickly to support critical business initiatives. You will own key pieces of the Cloud Compute infrastructure and be able to directly trace your work to meaningful business impact, all while working on extremely high-scale systems only found at a handful of companies.


Some examples of the team’s work can be found in tech blogs on “noisy neighbor” detection and mount lock contention.


What you will do:

  • Deliver compute platform capabilities and drive adoption across Netflix with a focus on engineering excellence, decisive execution,a spirit of bold experimentation, and tight alignment with business context.
  • You are an expert in building scalable and extensible compute platforms, and even better at working with other experts. You form strong cross-functional partnerships driven by trust, embracing a highly aligned and loosely coupled approach with many engineering teams, ensuring our solutions meet their needs while maintaining our focus on agility, scalability, reliability, and efficiency.
  • Set the example for operational excellence on the team and across Compute, continuously improving incident response, on-call, and other operational practices.
  • Maintain currency on, if not create, industry trends for new architectures, features, and off-the-shelf services; guide the team’s decision-making on incorporating industry trends.
  • You recognize industry trends early and stay ahead of them in new architectures, features, and off-the-shelf services, while guiding the team's decisions on when and how to adopt them. Identifying trends matters, but you go further: driven by a passion to learn from and contribute to the open-source world, you keep a pulse on it to shape and forecast the direction of technology.
  • Evangelize and embody Netflix’s culture 

Desired Skills & Experience:

  • A proven track record of architecting and implementing large-scale distributed systems that define and modify infrastructure at 100M+ user scale.
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with strong relationship-building ability.
  • Passion for technology and the ability to jump into an ambiguous area and break down complex problems.
  • Demonstrated technical leadership to empower the team around you and get the most from diverse stakeholders, including product managers, peer engineers across Netflix, and more.
  • Hands-on experience with Kubernetes and how to abstract away its' complexities.
  • Experience with Golang, Java, and/or Python.
  • Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, dynamic environment and manage multiple priorities effectively.

You will be successful in this role if you:

  • You enjoy operating in an environment where there are rarely obvious choices, and decision-making requires a balance of correctness, speed, and uncertainty. You have opinions but are also open to strong feedback.
  • You are able to execute strategically in the short-term while thinking long-term.
  • Have the ability to define and self-manage cross-functional projects fueled by ambiguous questions. 
  • You take pride in your work and the work your team delivers, and you always think at a team and business level. You bring an uncomfortably exciting mindset and are  comfortable with risk in pursuit of the exceptional.

    The Member Experience Client Foundations team builds the server-driven UI (SDUI) architecture and tooling that powers the member experience across Netflix's iOS, Android, and TV apps. You'll work with a modern Android stack (Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, Coroutines, Dagger/Hilt, GraphQL) and get exposure to problems that only show up at Netflix's scale: hundreds of millions of members, thousands of device types, and some of the largest live audiences on the internet.

  • You know there's rarely one “right” answer — you weigh trade-offs and make calls with incomplete information

Ads Data Engineering is at the core of building a data ecosystem that powers Netflix's understanding and decision-making about the impact of ads on our business. This team builds rich, connected, and easily accessible data products spanning ad inventory, forecasting, targeting, ad serving, pacing, measurement, and more.

We're looking for a Staff Data Engineer to help set the technical bar for the entire Ads DE org. This isn't a role focused on a single team or domain; it's about shaping how all of our ad data systems fit together, helping different teams land on coherent, scalable approaches, and serving as a thought partner to our engineering leaders as the business and data landscape continue to evolve.

Who are you?

  • A seasoned technologist with 15+ years building data-foundation, backend, or data engineering systems, someone other engineers naturally look to for direction.

  • You've spent real time in advertising or ad-tech data, and while your depth may run deepest in one domain, you're comfortable moving across several.

  • You've built trust and driven technical direction across organizational lines, not just within your own team, and you've done it in more than one company or role.

  • You've lived through the messy middle of a major platform migration or data products’ journey from 0 to 1 and 1 to 100, and you have the scars and the instincts to show for it.

  • You approach and design data as a product for the business with focus on users, quality, and measurable impact; You build data foundations as flywheels to unlock impact across the business, well beyond just orchestrating pipelines and serving analytics workflows.

  • You take data privacy and governance seriously, not as a checkbox, but as something you've actually built for.

  • You're a clear, thoughtful communicator who can translate technical nuance for engineers and business context for leaders, often in the same conversation.

  • You're comfortable with ambiguity, and just as comfortable helping a room of smart, opinionated engineers land on a shared answer.

  • You genuinely enjoy helping other engineers grow, and see that as just as core to the job as your own technical output.

What will you do?

  • Set technical direction and design coherence across the entire Ads Data Engineering org, connecting the dots between domains rather than optimizing just one.

  • Weigh in on and help resolve cross-domain design decisions, helping teams converge on approaches that scale across the org, not just within a single team.

  • Partner closely with the Ads DE director and DE managers as a senior technical voice, bridging technical strategy with broader business priorities.

  • Mentor and coach data engineers across the org, helping them grow technically and adopt AI and emerging tools and technologies.

  • Build strong partnerships with senior engineers on our data platform and D&I teams, contributing to and shaping horizontal and platform-wide efforts.

  • Help define what AI-native data engineering looks like for Ads DE as the function continues to evolve.

  • You will be the primary technical voice in partnerships with Ads Platform Engineering, Ads Data Science, and Product; Your impact will be at the Ads level, not at the sub-domain or pipeline-level.

  • Ad-tech systems and data flows, ideally with direct exposure to domains like bidding, measurement, or attribution.

Our team is new and yet faced with the enormous ambitions of building highly performant advertising systems and delivering high impact to our business by monetizing our incredible slate of content. As one of the newest entrants in the Connected TV advertising space that’s rapidly growing, we seek to build unique value propositions that help us differentiate from the competition and become a market leader in record time.

descriptionHtml:

This role will support the Publishing organization at Netflix, which includes our Tudum.com site, Podcasts, our Tudum Magazine and Written Communications. 

About Tudum.com
Tudum is your headquarters for the best of Netflix, no matter if you’re simply curious or a superfan. We give you inside access to the people and stories behind our shows and movies. Whether you’re fueling your passion for a long-standing favorite or finding your next obsession, Tudum makes watching Netflix better.

About Tudum Magazine
A print and digital publication that celebrates the people, the ideas, and the process of creating great entertainment on Netflix and beyond.

About Podcasts
Netflix Podcasts extend the conversation around Netflix and fuel fandom, allowing us to own our audience's time and redirect them to the service for more viewing.
Our goal is to ignite the power of Netflix fans – our biggest ambassadors and the engines of buzz about our titles. By leveraging multiple distribution platforms and collaborating with creative minds across the globe, Publishing at Netflix is all about connecting viewers with the stories they love, enhancing their experience, and driving engagement through innovative and immersive content.

The Role
We’re seeking a highly creative, strategic, and detail-oriented Photo/AV Curation Specialist to join Tudum’s Curation team within Netflix Publishing. This role will shape the visual expression of our stories across platforms by curating, editing, preparing, and placing photography, video, and motion assets that deepen storytelling and connect audiences with the titles and talent they love. Working across a wide range of formats and creative needs, this person will bring a strong editorial eye, technical fluency, and an understanding of how visual content can be thoughtfully packaged for Tudum and its off-platform channels.


You’ll uncover standout visuals across Netflix’s internal libraries, source and license imagery through external agencies, and create lightweight assets such as clips, GIFs, and stills that can stand alone or add dimension and impact to larger stories. You’ll also bring strong tooling literacy and a systems mindset, developing AI-assisted workflows, identifying opportunities to streamline production, and building repeatable solutions that help the team deliver high-quality creative work at scale.


Equal parts creative and technical, this role connects big-picture visual strategy with precise, hands-on execution across a high volume of work, including fast-moving entertainment news, trailer and first-look debuts, and original visual concepts that expand the worlds of Netflix films and series. The ideal candidate is a sharp visual storyteller, an inventive and systems-minded problem-solver, and an enthusiastic collaborator who thrives in a fast-paced, cross-functional environment.


Key Responsibilities

  • Research & Audience Consideration: Absorb as much information about a show or movie as possible to develop an informed point of view on how to approach visual storytelling on Tudum.com and its extensions off-platform.
  • Collaboration: Partner with the design, photo, video, and editorial teams to create innovative and immersive visual storytelling experiences that extend the worlds of some of Netflix’s most popular titles.
  • Cross-functional Communication: Distill ideas and project goals with collaborators outside of creative disciplines, including engineering and experience design teams.
  • Scale Creative Production Through AI-Assisted Workflows: Develop, test, and implement repeatable workflows that streamline production-focused tasks, improve creative efficiency, and enable the team to deliver high-quality work at scale.
  • Asset Choreography: Oversee rollout of visual assets for specific shows & films, from project greenlight through awards season on Tudum and Queue.
  • Visuals Research: Facilitate photo and video research and curation across external and internal asset banks.
  • Rights & Permissions: Secure rights/permissions for images, artwork, and video to support creative output & editorial storytelling.
  • Creative Review: Oversee the creative output of external vendors and freelancers to ensure work is delivered on time and to the Publishing org’s quality standards.
  • Post-Production: Supervise post production work on assets, including refining video clips, photo retouching, and managing rounds of feedback with internal and external stakeholders.
  • Advance Creative Tooling and Product Features: Partner with the Curation Manager to identify and champion improvements to the visual product experience, strengthen connections across internal creative tools, and create more seamless and efficient workflows.


Required Skills & Qualifications

  • 5+ years of experience working with multimedia formats and storytelling, preferably in the editorial or product space.
  • Familiarity with Adobe CC, specifically Photoshop, Bridge, Premiere, and After Effects.
  • Proven track record of integrating AI-driven efficiency tools into digital publishing pipelines to streamline asset management and content creation and iteration.
  • Experience and knowledge utilizing a wide variety of banks, databases, and agencies for stock, archival, and high-end portraiture needs.
  • Experience with digital asset management and content management systems.
  • Proven experience in creating pages for digital platforms, demonstrating a strong eye for design, visual pacing, and layout.
  • Highly motivated independent thinker with a goal-oriented mindset. Proactively generates new ideas, project plans, and solutions.
  • Strong organizational skills in work prioritization along with managing complex workflows, deadlines, and stakeholder communication. 
  • Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills, adept sharing ideas in a room or in writing to gain alignment with collaborators.

Preferred Skills & Qualifications

  • Data-comprehension skills to interpret performance metrics and use insights to fuel creative decision-making.
  • Experience with or a strong interest in exploring Generative AI (GenAI) technologies for use in creative development and production processes.

About the Role

We're looking for a Sr. Motion Designer who can move fluidly between 2D and 3D, and between concepting wide and finishing tight. You sketch ideas in motion before anyone else has committed to a direction, then carry that thinking all the way through to a polished, air-ready piece.


This is a hands-on craft role first: you're in the timeline, in the comp, building the work yourself. But when a look needs a decisive call fast, under a live deadline or a client in the room, you're comfortable stepping in to direct it and owning that call. Whether you're animating a bespoke 3D environment or finishing a 2D graphic package, the throughline is the same: motion that feels unmistakably Netflix.


What You’ll Do

  • Animate across 2D and 3D to bring brand DNA to life in motion, from quick concept sketches to fully finished pieces.
  • Concept wide before committing to a direction, then build the toolkits and systems that let that idea scale across a live show.
  • Extrapolate a creative vision into fully functional motion work, keeping technical excellence intact from first frame to final render.
  • Use new tools and emerging technology to move faster and push the visual quality of what you deliver.
  • Step in to direct a look when a call needs to be made fast, and finish the polished work yourself when it doesn't.

About You

  • You move naturally between 2D and 3D, and between concepting an idea and finishing it as final art.
  • You think wide before you commit, a "daydreamer" who can imagine the take before locking into one.
  • You're organized and disciplined in your files, so your work is a benefit, not a burden, to whoever picks it up next.
  • You can step in and direct a look under pressure when the moment calls for it, and hand it back once the direction is set.
  • You build inroads with cross-functional partners and stay a positive presence under a live deadline.

The Must-Haves

  • 10+ years of motion design experience across 2D and 3D, with a portfolio in high-end broadcast or live event work.
  • Strong command of both 2D and 3D animation, comfortable moving between After Effects and Cinema 4D as the work demands.
  • A portfolio demonstrating strong concept work as well as finished craft, proving you can originate a direction and execute it.
  • Proven ability to turn a flat design system into a dynamic, animated experience across formats.
  • Proven success using AI tools to speed up asset creation or exploration.
  • Comfortable stepping in to direct a look in a pinch without losing the ability to execute it yourself.
  • Deep technical understanding of render pipelines, finishing, and delivery for live broadcast.

Even Better

  • Experience with particle simulations, procedural tools, or advanced toolkitting across 2D/3D pipelines.
  • Studio art direction experience or designing in-venue AR/VR experiences.
  • Experience translating creative beyond the broadcast into Platform.

Why This Role Matters
This role brings the brand DNA to life in motion, moving fluidly between 2D and 3D so every live moment feels unmistakably Netflix. You're the one who can concept wide, execute with craft, and step into the director's chair when a look needs a fast, confident call. That range is what keeps our live properties moving as fast as the moments they're covering.

title: Language Producer,  Global English - Content Localization
locations: Los Angeles, California, United States of America
descriptionHtml:
At Netflix, our mission is to entertain the world. Together, we are writing the next episode - pushing the boundaries of storytelling, global fandom and making the unimaginable a reality. We are a dream team obsessed with the uncomfortable excitement of discovering what happens when you merge creativity, intuition and cutting-edge technology. Come be a part of what’s next.

Language Producers are the bridge between Netflix’s global content ambitions and the on-the-ground, in-market reality. They sit close to our members: in-region, speaking the language, understanding the culture, and translating data into meaningful, market-specific decisions. The Language Producer for Global English Content Localization is accountable for how members experience English-language localized audio, timed text, and marketing assets, ensuring Netflix customers across the globe get the highest-quality, most culturally resonant English localization — what a great time to join Netflix!

The Role

The Language Producer is a Content Localization expert accountable for language and partner health across English-language assets — the main liaison between Netflix and local dubbing, timed-text, and marketing localization vendors, and the execution arm of our partner strategy. This role is the first line of contact for local partners, focused on quality at scale rather than exhaustive title-by-title supervision. Success is measured by the health of the language and partner ecosystem, the role stewards, not by how many titles it personally touches.

This is a 60/40 role: roughly 60% of the time is spent strengthening the local partner ecosystem — vendor relationships, talent pipelines, training, and feedback loops — and 40% is spent on direct, tiered engagement with a curated slate of high-priority titles and assets. Partners are the first line of defense on execution; the Language Producer trains, aligns, and trusts them to meet Netflix’s quality bar, and steps in directly where judgment moves the needle most (in-market popularity, language expansion, new formats, or systemic quality signals). This is a demanding, fast-moving position that requires someone who can hold a strategic, ecosystem-level view while getting as tactical as necessary to deliver content, working across all components of English localization — dubbing, timed text, and marketing — alongside in-territory and cross-functional teams.

Responsibilities

PARTNER ECOSYSTEM MANAGEMENT (~60%)

  • Own the local relationship with English dubbing studios, timed-text and DL/PLDL vendors, and talent partners — run recurring tactical syncs and quarterly strategic reviews grounded in performance data, escalating global strategy, vetting, and contract matters to Global Resource Management (GRM).

  • Train, align, and support partners so they can consistently meet Netflix’s quality bar without relying on constant internal review; partners own day-to-day execution, and self-QC and local expertise are the default.

  • Build and grow talent pipelines and databases for English-language dubbing and audio description; identify casting gaps (mature voices, diverse casting, new AD narrators, niche genres) and design or sponsor initiatives with GRM to close them, monitoring progress against milestones.

  • Collaborate with partners on dubbing talent casting and mix reviews for select titles, while enforcing adherence to creative guidelines across all dubbed titles; look for opportunities to improve efficiency and innovation in budget, scheduling, and vendor mix.

  • Closely monitor union/guild activity, market rates, and the competitive landscape that could influence pricing, capacity, or general market behavior.

  • Act as a local integrator of partner and quality data and escalate critical local issues for visibility, even when the ultimate resolution sits with Legal or Public Policy.

TITLE-LEVEL ENGAGEMENT ACROSS WORKFLOWS (~40%, TIERED)

  • Apply a tiered support model across every asset type: engage directly (“Touch”) on the highest-priority titles for the market — roughly the top tier by in-market popularity, language expansion, or strategic slate — and rely on data and partner escalation (“Analysis”) for the rest of the slate.

  • Import assets (audio and timed text): for Touch titles, own material review (locked cut, context, terminology), creative and operational alignment with partners before work starts (casting, creative approach, scheduling), and creative review of final assets — including a pre-delivery watchdown of secondary audio and targeted timed-text QC — to validate outcomes and extract learnings that improve the wider ecosystem.

  • Same-language and pivot assets (OL forced narratives, SDH, PLDL/DL, English pivot templates): steward partner workflows and standards; align on the creative approach, terminology, and quality expectations for Touch titles; and use QC reports and spot checks to diagnose and address systemic gaps across the rest of the slate.

  • Main Title / Episode Title localization: own translation approval and oversight of vendor-suggested titles for Touch titles in English-speaking markets, and serve as the escalation point for linguistic questions on English MT/ET more broadly.

  • Marketing materials: conduct post-launch quality review of primary trailers for Touch titles; serve as an escalation point — not a systematic approver — for non-AV marketing assets like copy and taglines, in line with a predictable, ecosystem-focused workload.

  • Define standards of creative excellence and general creative guidelines for the market; conduct risk assessments for special upstream localization requests; and analyze content and language performance trends to address localization challenges in collaboration with Title Producers.

GUIDELINES STEWARDSHIP

  • Own and maintain language-specific style guides and creative guidelines (Timed Text Style Guides, Audio Description and DL/PLDL Style Guides, Creative Excellence Guidelines), keeping them current, accessible, and reflective of real production workflows.

  • Use guidelines as a primary tool for partner training, performance feedback, and quality interventions, and feed back learnings from title-level work to evolve them with new formats and workflows.

LANGUAGE & PARTNER HEALTH (QUALITY AT SOURCE)

  • Diagnose language health using metrics, QC/TQ signals, and member feedback; translate findings into a market-level strategy — where quality is strong versus where systemic intervention or training is needed.

  • Track vendor performance over time to inform smart routing, training priorities, and vendor-mix decisions, with the goal of reducing reliance on third-party QC as partner quality matures.

INNOVATION & AUTOMATION

  • Stay current on how technology — ASR, machine translation, TQ models, and automation — is reshaping the localization process, and help define “fit-for-purpose” quality standards by format and tier as the company’s strategy develops.

  • Act as subject matter expert for localization workflows in English, supporting the Dubbing Strategy and Innovation roadmap and Netflix’s tooling ecosystem to drive vendor adoption.

  • Participate in tests and quality control of lip sync, VO, machine translation, and core asset roll-outs; feed structured feedback back to Strategy & Innovation (S&I) and algorithm teams rather than treating model outputs as a black box.

CROSS-FUNCTIONAL COLLABORATION

  • Initiate, support, and collaborate with cross-functional partners on Inclusion and Diversity initiatives to keep strategy consistent across the organization.

  • Be sensitive to the local competitive landscape and maintain a working knowledge of localization contracts and local best practices between talent and Netflix’s vendors.

Requirements

  • A minimum of 5–10 years of dubbing and/or timed-text title/language management experience (creative and operations).

  • Based in Los Angeles, CA, with a willingness to travel internationally and the flexibility to work across time zones to support a globally distributed team.

  • Ability to inspire trust and build teams while representing Netflix professionally to partners.

  • Curiosity about innovation and the ability to adapt to new technologies and processes, including automation and AI-driven quality tooling.

  • Comfort reading and questioning data and dashboards (QC/TQ metrics, partner ratings) to drive decisions — this does not require a data science background, but does require the ability to connect metrics to member experience and turn them into vendor action.

  • A strong understanding of localization workflows and pipelines, including real-time workflows, and the ability to execute titles at various points of production (development through delivery).

  • Experience navigating complex vendor relationships, including difficult conversations about quality, accountability, and automation.

  • Highly analytical, able to identify root causes and propose changes to existing workflows; adept at writing, facilitating, and presenting analyses.

  • Familiarity with (or willingness to learn) English-language localization contracts, union/guild dynamics, and local market best practices.

  • Bachelor’s degree preferred and/or equivalent, relevant work experience.

  • Native fluency in English is mandatory; proficiency in another language is beneficial.

title: Manager, Engineering - AI Search Platform
locations: Warsaw, Poland
descriptionHtml:
Netflix is one of the world's leading entertainment services, with over 300 million paid memberships in over 190 countries enjoying TV series, films and games across a wide variety of genres and languages. Members can play, pause and resume watching as much as they want, anytime, anywhere, and can change their plans at any time.

About the organization

Content Infrastructure & Solutions (CIS) empowers engineers working on content, studio and enterprise applications to be innovative and agile in supporting Netflix's global content production needs. We do that by providing scalable and resilient infrastructure for large-scale media, assets, data, workflow and communication use cases.

Connected Enterprise Foundations (CEF), part of CIS, provides highly leveraged and fully managed data, search, workflow and messaging platforms for Content, Studio and Enterprise Engineering. CEF's charter is a connected enterprise experience: consistent, composable platform primitives that application teams and their agents build on, rather than a collection of separate products each with its own model of the world. Our sibling teams include Knowledge Foundations (data and domain modeling), Eventing and Communications Platform, Enterprise Workflow Platform, and the Enterprise Developer Paved Road.

About the team and the role

The AI Search Platform team owns Graph Search, Netflix’s enterprise search-as-a-service platform. Graph Search provides engineering teams with a unified way to index, search, and resolve entities across Content, Studio, Ads, and Enterprise. The team also builds and operates capabilities that enable internal users and agents to access the graph through natural language. It partners closely with the Knowledge Foundations team on the Unified Data Architecture, Data Dictionary, and Entity Graph.

The platform operates at significant scale today:

  • Approximately 19,500 weekly active users, more than double year over year

  • 13.5 million API calls per day, up 97% year over year

  • 233 production indices containing 13.3 billion documents, with index count up 74% year over year

  • More than 200 client applications consuming the search API, more than double year over year

You will lead a team of eight engineers based in Warsaw. The team has deep end-to-end ownership of the platform: it operates its own on-call, has delivered order-of-magnitude latency improvements across indexing and query paths, and has developed AI-powered operational tooling that has been adopted by other CIS teams.

The platform is at an inflection point, which makes this role particularly important:

  • From service to self-service. Graph Search is a powerful platform, but adoption is not yet effortless. Multi-tenancy, data product integration, and self-service onboarding are the next major steps.

  • From applications to primitives. The team has deliberately chosen not to build standalone end-user applications. Instead, it provides composable search primitives that enable other teams to build their own products, agents, and experiences while the team owns the underlying platform. Defining and maintaining that boundary, including evaluating when a use case does not belong on the platform, is a key part of the role.

  • Advance agentic and semantic search without neglecting the core. Agents are becoming first-class consumers of search, and semantic retrieval and entity grounding are major areas of investment. At the same time, keyword search remains the largest source of user value. The challenge is to advance the platform for emerging AI use cases without under-investing in the fundamentals that users depend on today.

  • Build a stronger discipline around impact. The team has an opportunity to become much more rigorous in connecting its investments to measurable business and organizational outcomes. Prioritization should be evidence-backed rather than strictly driven by inbound requests. You’ll also have the opportunity to shape how the team prioritizes its work and measures success.

To learn more about what the team does, check out the following tech blogs written by the team:

  • How Netflix Content Engineering makes a federated graph searchable

  • How Netflix Content Engineering makes a federated graph searchable (Part 2)

  • Reverse Searching Netflix’s Federated Graph

  • The AI Evolution of Graph Search at Netflix: From Structured Queries to Natural Language

What you will do

You will lead a team of software engineers to deliver high-impact results. In this role you will:

  • Be a thought partner to the product manager, engineers, and engineering managers across Netflix engineering in setting the vision, strategy, and adoption path for Search, natural-language search, and Smart Tables as platform capabilities. Ensure we build the capabilities that enable engineering teams across Netflix to design and ship AI search solutions at scale.

  • Collaborate closely with Knowledge Foundations and the broader CEF organization to align roadmaps across Graph Search, Entity Graph, Data Dictionary, Unified Data Architecture, and Communications Platform, so stakeholders experience a coherent set of capabilities rather than adjacent products.

  • Serve as a credible technical advisor to the team, helping engineers make thoughtful, well-informed decisions in complex and ambiguous situations.

  • Raise the team’s rigor around impact. Define meaningful leading indicators, ask stakeholders for evidence behind their requests, and deprioritize work that does not demonstrate sufficient value.

  • Own the operational excellence of a Tier 1 platform, including 24x7 on-call responsibilities, capacity and performance headroom, infrastructure-level data validation, observability, and SLOs that help prevent predictable outages rather than discover limits through incidents. Flexible scheduling or coverage accommodations can be supported where appropriate.

  • Drive AI-first ways of working across the team, both by treating agents as first-class consumers of the platform and by advancing agent-assisted engineering practices, supported by the code review, change-risk management, testing, and evaluation practices required to use them safely at scale.

  • Build trusted relationships with partners and stakeholders, connect opportunities across teams to maximize business impact, and prioritize work beyond the boundaries of your immediate domain when it benefits the broader organization.

  • Communicate complex technical and product ideas clearly through written and verbal channels and influence decisions across a diverse set of stakeholders.

  • Balance near-term business needs with strong engineering principles by investing in foundational technical work, paying down technical debt, and making incremental improvements that deliver timely results while strengthening the platform over time.

  • Lead, hire, coach, and develop a team of engineers. Challenge them to perform effectively, expand their ownership, and grow their impact beyond their immediate scope.

  • Foster a strong culture of accountability and help the team deliver reliably and predictably for critical business stakeholders.

  • Build and nurture an inclusive team culture where every team member feels empowered, respected, and able to contribute at their best.

What we are looking for

  • Experience building and operating highly reliable platform systems that support large-scale, business-critical use cases, including 24x7 on-call responsibilities and highly available, low-latency services.

  • Strong technical acumen in distributed systems, with the ability to move between implementation details and broader architectural strategy. You will represent the team’s technical decisions credibly, evaluate assumptions, and maintain strong engineering standards.

  • Experience building and leading inclusive teams. Ability to attract and retain talent, ensure diverse perspectives inform decisions, and foster a culture of accountability where individuals take ownership while contributing to the team’s collective success.

  • Ability to create an environment of open, direct communication where team members feel comfortable giving constructive feedback, recognizing strong performance, and addressing areas that need improvement.

  • Strong long-term strategic thinking and a platform mindset, with the ability to define and articulate a clear product and technical vision and connect it to the broader objectives of the organization.

  • Ability to prioritize strategically, align the team’s investments with larger business goals, and change direction when new evidence or broader impact warrants it.

  • Rigor in decision making and the ability to reduce ambiguity through the right combination of data, stakeholder input, constructive dissent, and targeted experiments or pilot investments.

  • Experience working effectively with product managers and TPMs, building trust and collaborating on both strategic vision and project execution.

  • Strong partnership and influencing skills across engineering partners and stakeholders, including demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively across globally distributed teams and time zones.

  • A track record of helping teams deliver critical priorities reliably amid competing demands, while partnering with product and engineering leaders to shape where investment should go.

  • Fluency with AI-assisted engineering and a clear point of view on how engineering teams should adopt it safely at scale, including thoughtful practices around review, testing, change risk, and engineering quality.

Nice to have
