title: Technical Infrastructure Delivery - Network Deployment Manager
locations: Los Angeles, California, United States of America
Los Gatos, California, United States of America
descriptionHtml:
At Netflix, our mission is to entertain the world. Together, we are writing the next episode - pushing the boundaries of storytelling, global fandom and making the unimaginable a reality. We are a dream team obsessed with the uncomfortable excitement of discovering what happens when you merge creativity, intuition and cutting-edge technology. Come be a part of what’s next.

Open Connect is Netflix's content delivery network, built to deliver a seamless experience to our members and internal teams alike. Within Open Connect Deployment, our Technical Infrastructure Delivery (TID) team designs and deploys the network infrastructure that powers Netflix's global offices and creative spaces, giving our business and creative teams the connectivity they need to do their best work.

TID's mission is to drive the successful deployment and management of network infrastructure and low-voltage systems across Netflix's offices and creative spaces, supporting the strategic initiatives that expand Netflix's technological capabilities. The team sits at the intersection of business strategy, network engineering, infrastructure design, and construction, partnering with Open Connect functions, cross-functional tech teams, and internal stakeholders

This role calls for someone who is detail-oriented and an effective multitasker, able to prioritize competing project demands, remain solution-oriented, and think dynamically. This person will be the driving strategic influence behind network infrastructure deployments that directly support creative and corporate business initiatives, managing internal teams' time and expertise for maximum impact and keeping tactical and strategic efforts aligned across the org. This individual will own the layer 1 structured cabling design and integration process end-to-end, translating TID's strategy into delivered, working infrastructure for each space.

A successful candidate bridges the gap between our partners' needs and the resources and information required for successful network delivery and ongoing operational excellence. This person is a strong communicator who acts as the technical liaison on each project, connecting the technical teams that deploy and support our networks with the business stakeholders, partners, and end users who consume them. They work closely with our design and construction project teams throughout each build, serving as the handoff point between our organization and the teams we partner with and support.

Qualifications:

  • 8+ years of technical project/program management experience, including deploying networks or other technical infrastructure solutions.

  • Strong strategic planning skills, with the ability to develop a network deployment strategy that aligns with Netflix's broader organizational goals, weigh short-term delivery needs against long-term opportunity, and adjust plans as business priorities and resources shift.

  • Act as technical liaison and build strong relationships between engineers, business stakeholders, and technical leaders, partnering to deliver global network programs, including remediations, integrations, and new deployment models.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with sound judgment on when, how, and what to communicate to technical and non-technical partners alike

  • Lead end-to-end program and project management for network infrastructure deployments, scoping resource requirements, building schedules and budgets, coordinating logistics, and running progress checks to hold projects accountable against deliverables and deadlines.

  • Own low-voltage infrastructure and Layer 1 design and delivery, managing design and integration vendors through the full project lifecycle (schematic design, design development, construction documents, procurement, installation, commissioning, and documentation), reviewing vendor work against TID's basis of design, and evolving our guidelines based on tactical learnings.

  • Coordinate and hold accountable internal and external design and construction teams, including project managers, architects, general contractors, low-voltage design and integration vendors, mechanical/electrical contractors, and AV/security engineers.

  • AI-first approach to shape workflows, address complex work, and build repeatable patterns to scale resources.

  • Comfort operating in a fast-paced, ambiguous, and constantly changing environment.

  • Ability to work across time zones and travel as needed.

Generally, our compensation structure consists solely of an annual salary; we do not have bonuses. You choose each year how much of your compensation you want in salary versus stock options. Our Team

We're looking for a Product Manager to own the strategy, roadmap, and execution for billing and financial workflows on our ad tech platform — including how we design AI-assisted billing automation with the right human checkpoints built in from day one.


Job Responsibilities

  • Own the product strategy and roadmap for billing and financial workflows across CTV ad revenue: impression/ad-slot reconciliation, invoicing, revenue recognition support, discrepancy resolution, and dispute handling across demand partners, ad networks, and direct advertisers

title: Senior Software Engineer 5  — Validation & Safety Platform
locations: Warsaw, Poland
descriptionHtml:
Netflix is one of the world's leading entertainment services, with over 300 million paid memberships in over 190 countries enjoying TV series, films and games across a wide variety of genres and languages. Members can play, pause and resume watching as much as they want, anytime, anywhere, and can change their plans at any time.

About the team


The Validation & Safety Platform is one of three pillars inside the new System Health, Validation & Insights Platform group in Productivity Engineering. Our mandate: catch safety and correctness regressions in human-written or agent-generated code before they reach production.


Netflix's agent fleet now writes, tests, refactors, and deploys code continuously across every domain. As agent volume grows, the constraint shifts from producing changes to knowing which ones are safe. Quality assurance can no longer be a human-gated step at the end of a PR — it has to be embedded at every stage of the developer loop, proactive and automated.


Today the team runs the validation and safety gates for the fleet: automated test generation, coverage and safeguards show teams where they stand. We're extending to other safety signals built specifically for agent-generated code, so we can judge whether a change is genuinely correct as agents write and modify code at scale.


About the role


We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer to help build the next generation of this platform: tools and guardrails that keep pace with an engineering org where a growing share of code is agent-generated.


You will design systems that thousands of engineers and their agents depend on, make build-vs-extend calls on what the platform should own versus expose through an API, and bring a security-conscious view to how autonomous agents get sandboxed, scoped, and safely given access to test infrastructure.


Key responsibilities


  • Design and build validation and safety products used platform-wide: test generation, coverage and safeguards, deterministic and predictive test selection, and mutation testing at scale.
  • Build the polyglot static analysis layer that gives agent-generated code an automated, language-agnostic first quality gate.
  • Develop agent-specific safety signals: detect prompt flakiness (an agent producing inconsistent output across identical prompts or seeds), evaluate agent trajectories against execution traces, and score semantic correctness of agent-generated code against the original requirement, the agent's own stated intent, and observed behavior change.
  • Define clear platform capabilities and make deliberate build-vs-buy, build-vs-extend calls as the platform's scope grows.
  • Apply sound judgment on agent sandboxing, scoping, and data redaction wherever the platform gives agents access to test infrastructure or execution environments.

Who you are


  • Experienced building and operating a platform used by other engineering teams — you think about your product as a platform, not a one-off tool.
  • Comfortable making product calls: what capability the platform should own, what it should expose as an API, and when to extend versus build new.
  • An advanced user of agentic coding tools — you work daily with hooks, MCPs, and context management, even if you haven't built an agentic platform yourself.
  • Security-minded: you have a working understanding of agent sandboxing, scoping, and redaction, even if it isn't your primary background.
  • A strong communicator who can document technical tradeoffs clearly for both engineering and non-technical stakeholders.
  • An advocate for a strong testing culture: familiar with test frameworks, code coverage tooling, CI systems, and post-deployment verification.

Experience we'd be excited about


  • You have designed or operated developer-platform infrastructure: distribution, CI/CD, or versioning systems used by many teams.
  • You have built or integrated LLM-based evaluation systems (LLM-as-judge, agent trajectory scoring, or similar).
  • You have worked with mutation testing, static analysis, or test-selection systems at scale.
  • You have hands-on experience sandboxing or scoping agent access to sensitive systems or data.

Netflix is one of the world's leading entertainment services, with over 300 million paid memberships in over 190 countries enjoying TV series, films and games across a wide variety of genres and languages. We are looking for an experienced and inspiring Marketing leader who demonstrates enthusiasm for Netflix and has the intellectual curiosity and emotional intelligence to effectively lead and collaborate with a diverse and talented team, as well as other ANZ and global leaders.

They will manage a local team responsible for creating and executing marketing strategies leveraging our brand and content to drive awareness, engagement and conversation that puts Netflix to be in the cultural zeitgeist and at the heart of Aussie and Kiwi culture. They will also be a part of the APAC marketing leadership team, and will work closely with their colleagues across the region. The leader will bring sharp, sophisticated, and innovative thinking to the team while focusing on operational excellence both internally (execution, cross-functional collaboration) and externally (bold creative assets, holistic consumer campaigns, & beneficial partnerships). 

The Director of Marketing, ANZ will be based in Sydney.


Success Factors

  • Strategic Marketer that can orchestrate across disciplines: Experience in the creation and execution of comprehensive marketing strategies independently, and can orchestrate transversely across disciplines reporting into them (Title Marketing, Social marketing, Events, Publicity, Photo & AV studio) and those not reporting directly to them (Consumer Products, Partner Marketing, Brand, Media Strategy and Buying, etc)

Ability to analyze both market trends and customer insights to identify opportunities for growth, innovation, and member joy.
  • Excellent Leadership Skills: Coach and empower team members, foster a collaborative and productive work environment to achieve goals. Has proven ability to inspire a diverse set of functional leaders. Leaders at Netflix are not top-down managers. You will be expected to lead by example in alignment with our company values; where you will be expected to provide Context, not Control, giving guidance to your team but also the space and support to thrive at Netflix.
  • Team Builder: Organizational development capabilities, demonstrating team-building and skills development.
  • Humble Integrity: has the instinct to do the “right” thing, is selfless and always has good intent. 
  • Executive Presence: can “own” a room and influence positively; equally knows when it is needed vs not
  • High Impact Engagement with other leaders in the organization; building relationships from a distance comes naturally to them
  • Cultivator of New Ideas: pushes for innovation and not afraid to take calculated risks
  • Strong Growth Mindset: demonstrates agility and adapts as the environment changes

Experience & Skills

title: Project Manager, Creative Innovation

descriptionHtml:

We are a dream team obsessed with the uncomfortable excitement of discovering what happens when you merge creativity, intuition and cutting-edge technology. Come be a part of what’s next.


About the Role

Netflix's Creative Innovation team works at the intersection of storytelling and emerging technology, shaping how solutions like Generative AI influence production practices across the Studio and the broader industry. This role sits at the center of that work.


You will own the operational backbone of that work: scoping engagements, building budgets, aligning stakeholders, and communicating with vendors so that every project run through this program has the same rigor and discipline as any other production, even while the work itself is experimental. You'll be the first point of contact for productions and vendors alike, translating what's technically possible into a clear plan a title can actually execute against, and you'll keep leadership and stakeholders informed with clean, credible reporting on status, risk, and progress.


This is a role for someone who is energized by operational ownership in ambiguous territory: comfortable quickly grasping new and emerging technologies, credible with executives, creators, and vendors, and able to bring order to work that, by nature, doesn't have a template yet.


Key Responsibilities

  • Help scope and stand up new engagements. Define budgets, timelines, and stakeholder alignment at kickoff so each project starts with a clear plan.
  • Serve as the primary point of contact for engaged productions. Keep title managers and filmmakers informed on scope, timeline, and what this program's involvement means for their production, from kickoff through wrap.
  • Communicate with and project manage vendors. Assist in setting expectations, conduct recurring check-ins, monitor pacing and quality, and identify opportunities for continued development or maturity graduation.
  • Partner with leadership on project sourcing. Evaluate candidate titles, manage identified project risk, compare investment opportunities, and justify selections against program criteria.
  • Handle the legal and contracting logistics of each engagement. Confirm that creator agreements and vendor paperwork are completed before funded work begins.
  • Report on program status and performance. Synthesize feedback and sentiment gathered across regions into clear updates for stakeholders and senior leadership.
  • Produce the materials that document the program's work. Build project recaps, summaries, and presentations for productions and leadership.

What We're Looking For

  • 6+ years of experience in production coordination or production management, with ownership of budgets, timelines, and status tracking across multiple concurrent projects.
  • Experience coordinating with external vendors, including setting expectations and identifying issues early.
  • Comfortable quickly grasping and speaking credibly about new and emerging creative technologies, even without prior specialized expertise, and translating capabilities and limitations into practical rollout plans.
  • Clear, direct communicator who can flex naturally between executives, creators, and vendors.
  • Comfortable operating within an innovation space, pivoting quickly, and living comfortably with ambiguity.
  • Strong writing and presentation skills, including deck building and narrative synthesis.
  • High integrity and discretion with sensitive creator, vendor, and internal information.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with virtual production, volumetric capture, or VFX workflows.
  • Existing familiarity with the generative AI landscape (image, video, audio) and how productions evaluate and adopt these tools.
  • Exposure to vendor or technology partner evaluation frameworks.
  • Experience working across international productions or regional teams.

title: Business Security Partner (L5)
locations: Remote, United States
descriptionHtml:
At Netflix, our mission is to entertain the world. Together, we are writing the next episode - pushing the boundaries of storytelling, global fandom and making the unimaginable a reality. We are a dream team obsessed with the uncomfortable excitement of discovering what happens when you merge creativity, intuition and cutting-edge technology. Come be a part of what’s next.

The Team

Netflix’s Business Security Partner (BSP) team is a team of senior security advisors organized around business proximity rather than technical domains. Each BSP partner owns relationships with a defined portfolio of business units, builds long-term relationships with BU leadership, and serves as the security export who understands those businesses well enough to advise on decisions before they are made. We sit in business reviews, participate in architecture conversations, and build the kind of trust with stakeholders that makes security a resource rather than a requirement. 


Across all of our relationships, the goal is the same: every major business decision at Netflix should have access to clear, usable security risk context; not a compliance output buried in a document, but actionable guidance from a partner who understands both the risk and the business. 


About the Role

This role covers two distinct, fast-moving areas within Netflix: Marketing and Animation.  BSP aligns coverage based on need and often rotates business units. You may cover other areas during your time at Netflix. BSP right-sizes risk while enabling business outcomes. 


On the Marketing side, you will be the primary security partner for teams spanning Consumer Products, Brand, Events, Experiences, and Social Media, as well as the external agency and vendor ecosystems that touch pre-release campaign content. You will advise on the security risk of GenAI tools Marketing teams are actively building and adopting, assess vendors and Business Process Outsourcing partners handling sensitive creative assets, and govern the access controls that protect Netflix’s social media accounts. 


For Animation, you will partner with Netflix Animation as its dedicated security partner. Your work will span security risk assessment of the animation production pipeline, advancing the alignment of legacy systems with Netflix standards, and advising on architectural decisions that affect how pre-release animated content is protected. The pace of change is high, both in the business and in the legacy integration work. Your ability to engage credibly with engineering and leadership on complex, technically interdependent risk is essential.


This role also carries M&A responsibilities. BSPs at Netflix are expected to support technical security due diligence for acquisitions and subsidiaries. 


What You Will Work On:

  • Own the security partnership for Marketing and Animation, building stakeholder relationships, learning how these businesses operate, and translating that context into opinionated security guidance.
  • Lead security risk assessments and treatment strategies with cross-functional teams as they launch new capabilities and tools.
  • Evaluate and advise on the security risk of GenAI tool adoption across both business units. Set conditions of approval, assess training data provenance and data handling, and partner with Legal and Privacy on unified guidance. 
  • Maintain and evolve the Business Risk Profile for each business unit, prioritizing and driving remediation of the risks that matter most.
  • Advance pre-release content protection in partnership across both business units: campaign assets and creative content in Marketing, and animation production pipelines and studio workstation environments. Coordinate with Content Security and partner SPA teams to ensure controls match the sensitivity of what’s in scope. 
  • Support M&A technical security due diligence for acquisitions and subsidiaries. 
  • Develop reporting and metrics that communicate risk posture and business security initiatives to SPA leadership and business unit stakeholders.

Desired Background:

  • Experience operating as a security partner or advisor. You’ve built trust with business stakeholders, translated technical risk into business language, and driven decisions without direct authority. 
  • GenAI security depth. You have direct experience advising on or assessing security risks in GenAI systems. You can identify real risks and engage credibly with technical teams, legal, and privacy partners to mitigate them. 
  • Broad security domain knowledge across application security, cloud security, identity and access management, and data governance. You are comfortable operating across all of them and know when to go deep versus when to synthesize, practicing business awareness on how to communicate.  You pull in domain experts from across the wider security organization, where needed, to help assess and address risks. 
  • Strong stakeholder partnership instincts. You build trust with the business by demonstrating that you understand their context, not just their security posture. You know how to translate a technical finding into a business decision, and back to the Security department for support. 
  • Comfort with ambiguity and novel technology environments. You have a framework for reasoning under uncertainty and for making recommendations when the answer isn't fully known.
  • M&A or technical due diligence experience is a plus and not required.

title: Engineering Manager — Change Systems
locations: Warsaw, Poland
descriptionHtml:
Netflix is one of the world's leading entertainment services, with over 300 million paid memberships in over 190 countries enjoying TV series, films and games across a wide variety of genres and languages. Members can play, pause and resume watching as much as they want, anytime, anywhere, and can change their plans at any time.

About the Organization

Platform Modernization Engineering (PME) helps keep Netflix's engineering fleet healthy, secure, and current. We design and run the large-scale migration and modernization campaigns that move the fleet forward — from dependency upgrades to infrastructure-level changes — so that individual engineering teams don't have to absorb that toil on their own.

About the Team and the Role

The Change Systems team owns the platforms that make fleet-wide change possible at Netflix.  It gives engineering teams across the company a unified way to scope, launch, automate, and validate change at scale — from routine dependency updates to complex, multi-service migrations — with as little manual toil as possible.

The platform already operates at significant scale: over 100 engineering teams run change activities across thousands of repositories, and usage continues to grow year over year. The team's mandate is expanding to match — pushing automation further using AI-assisted code modification, rule-based transformations, and batch orchestration. The goal is to make the majority of change at Netflix low-to-no-effort for the engineers on the receiving end, while giving the teams driving that change the tooling, telemetry, and adoption data they need to move with confidence.


You will lead the engineers who build and operate this platform, based in Warsaw. This is a team with deep end-to-end ownership: they run their own on-call, design the automation and orchestration layers directly, and are pushing the platform toward AI-driven code transformation as a first-class capability rather than a one-off tool. 

End-to-end ownership translates into several responsibilities:

  • From a technical perspective, acting like a System Architect, driving technical architecture and component integration; 
  • From a product perspective, wearing the Product Manager hat for Campaigns and defining the vision and strategy for the Campaigns experience; 
  • From a partnership and stakeholders' perspective, identifying needs, incorporating feedback, aligning across the organization, creating partnerships to drive impact
  • From a leadership perspective, acting like a Change Agent and Advocate supporting the overall organization in shaping the mindset and approach around Campaigns (change at scale) in the agentic world; 

The platform is at an inflection point, which makes this role particularly important:

  • From tooling to platform. Change Systems has built strong point solutions for individual campaigns. The next step is composable, declarative abstractions that every part of the platform — and the teams building on top of it — share a common foundation rather than one-off automation.
  • From manual campaign design to AI-assisted execution. GenAI-driven code transformation, contract-based validation, and batch orchestration are becoming core to how campaigns get executed — across code transformation, CI, testing, and delivery to production.
  • From reactive to metrics-driven prioritization. Using historical campaign completion data to predict bottlenecks, target specific automation investments, and measure adoption and adherence rather than simply responding to inbound requests.
  • From isolated campaigns to a coherent customer experience. Close technical alignment is required with Source Management, Continuous Integration, Resilience Engineering and Delivery Engineering and Security so that campaign recipients experience one coherent platform, not a patchwork of tools.

What You Will Do

  • Be a thought partner to Organization Champions, Campaign Managers, Campaign Recipients, and engineering leadership in setting the vision, strategy, and adoption path for fleet-wide change management as a platform capability.
  • Own the technical architecture direction for a composable, declarative platform that generalizes beyond any single migration use case.
  • Serve as a credible technical advisor to your team, helping engineers navigate ambiguous, cross-domain technical decisions — and act as the team's escalation point for novel campaigns that span multiple technical domains.
  • Drive AI-first ways of working across the team: treat AI-assisted code modification as core infrastructure, and advance agent-assisted engineering practices with the code review, change-risk management, testing, and evaluation rigor required to run them safely at scale.
  • Raise the team's rigor around impact — define meaningful adoption and adherence metrics, use historical campaign data to predict and target automation investment, and prioritize based on evidence rather than only inbound requests.
  • Own the operational excellence of a platform relied on across the fleet, including on-call responsibilities, telemetry and dashboards for fleet health, and feedback loops that continuously improve campaign design and execution.
  • Communicate complex technical and product tradeoffs clearly, in writing and verbally, to influence decisions across a broad set of stakeholders — including technical executives, SREs, and security incident commanders.
  • Lead, hire, coach, and develop a team of engineers; challenge them to expand their ownership and grow their impact beyond their immediate scope.
  • Foster a strong culture of accountability, and build an inclusive team environment where every engineer feels empowered to contribute at their best.

What We Are Looking For

  • Experience building and operating platform systems that support large-scale, business-critical use cases, including on-call responsibilities and resilient, well-instrumented services.
  • Strong technical acumen in distributed systems and developer platforms, with the ability to move between architecture and implementation detail, and to represent technical decisions credibly to partner teams.
  • Experience building and leading inclusive engineering teams, attracting and retaining talent, and fostering a culture where individuals take ownership while contributing to shared outcomes.
  • Strong long-term strategic thinking and a platform mindset — able to define a technical vision for composable, extensible systems and connect it to broader organizational goals.
  • Proven ability to navigate ambiguity, influence without authority, and partner effectively with senior stakeholders across engineering, product, and security.
  • Rigor in decision-making: comfortable reducing ambiguity through a mix of data, stakeholder input, constructive dissent, and targeted experiments.
  • Fluency with AI-assisted engineering, with a clear point of view on how to adopt GenAI-driven code transformation and agentic tooling safely at scale.
  • Strong technical writing skills — design docs, tradeoff analyses, postmortems — and a track record of driving complex, cross-functional technical projects from design through completion.

Nice to Have

  • Experience with large-scale code migration or modernization campaigns.
  • Experience building or operating fleet-management, dependency graph, or service catalog systems.
  • Background in platform or infrastructure engineering organizations.
  • Familiarity with Java or Python in a backend services context.
  • Experience designing platforms where agents, not just humans, are first-class consumers — including provisioning and debugging through APIs rather than a UI.
  • Experience with cloud infrastructure (AWS preferred: EC2, S3, EKS/Kubernetes).

descriptionHtml:

Media Science DSE is hiring for an embedded role to stand up our data science capability within NAS. How well NAS plans for and manages its growing slate and workforce has a direct impact on the creative and financial success of its films. As a Data Scientist, you'll construct and execute the roadmap for analysis, models, and data products that connect finance, production, and people data into a single system empowering slate planning, operational forecasting, and strategic decision-making for the Studio. You'll work directly with NAS leadership across Studio Operations and Production to architect the robust data foundations NAS needs to scale its slate with confidence.


As a Senior Data Scientist in this space, you will…

  • Serve as NAS's founding data scientist, partnering with leadership to define and prioritize the studio's metrics & science agenda

title: Crowds Supervisor - Netflix Animation Studios
locations: Vancouver, Canada
descriptionHtml:
Netflix Animation Studios is on a mission to entertain the world with bold, immersive animated films that are timeless and impactful. We are paving the way for the future of animation by building a community of amazing artists and talent across three vibrant locations globally. Come join us!

Job Summary:


We are seeking a Crowds Supervisor to support our upcoming feature film. The Crowds Supervisor works inside of NAS to lead the crowds team on a specific film, overseeing character crowds simulations, background performances, and large-scale crowds moments. This role ensures that crowds support the story’s scale, tone, and visual style and are technically robust for downstream departments.


What You’ll Do:


  • Depending on the project scope, lead and mentor a team of crowds artists and TDs, which may include assigning work appropriately and providing clear, constructive feedback in dailies and reviews.
  • Collaborate with the VFX Supervisor, Head of Character Effects, Head of Effects, Head of Character Animation, and other show leadership to interpret crowds briefs and define the visual and technical standards for crowds across the show.
  • Supervise crowds work on shots and sequences, ensuring that crowds behaviour, scale, and staging support story clarity, performance, and cinematic composition.
  • Create or refine selected crowds setups, cycles, and/or shots as needed—particularly complex, hero, or reference‑setting work—to help establish the quality bar, style, and technical approach for the team.
  • Collaborate directly with the Animation Supervisor to determine crowds cycle needs, helping to inform requirements and working to maintain cycle standards.
  • Work closely with Assets, Layout, Environments, Effects, CFX, Lighting, and Compositing to ensure crowds integrate seamlessly into shots and support hero action and readability.
  • Help define and refine crowd tools, workflows, and libraries in partnership with Technical Supervisors, crowds TDs, and pipeline teams.
  • Provide input to Production Management and department leadership on crowds complexity and progress to support realistic planning and prioritization.
  • Troubleshoot technical and artistic challenges in crowds work, collaborating on solutions that maintain quality while meeting schedule needs.
  • Help foster a respectful, inclusive, and collaborative team culture where artists and TDs can do their best work.

What You’ll Need:


  • Significant experience in crowds or character effects work for feature animation, VFX, or high‑end series, including time in a Lead or Supervisory role.
  • A strong reel demonstrating high-quality crowds systems and simulations, and their integration into complex sequences.
  • Proficiency with crowds and simulation tools such as Houdini (and/or proprietary crowds systems), with familiarity in other DCCs, e.g., Maya, Golaem or Massive is a plus.
  • Strong understanding of how crowd work interacts with Animation, Layout, Environments, FX, CFX, Lighting, and Compositing within a production pipeline.
  • Excellent communication and leadership skills, with the ability to give clear, constructive feedback and collaborate effectively across departments.
  • Strong organizational and problem‑solving skills.

This role is based in Vancouver, British Columbia. Hybrid Role (Minimum of 3 days a week in the office).

locations: Vancouver, Canada
descriptionHtml:
Netflix Animation Studios is on a mission to entertain the world with bold, immersive animated films that are timeless and impactful. We are paving the way for the future of animation by building a community of amazing artists and talent across three vibrant locations globally. Come join us!

Job Summary:


Are you interested in working on Netflix Animation Studios’ next animated feature with our highly talented team of artists? We are looking for Environment Modeling Artists who love building appealing, stylized environments and assets, from strong architectural proportions and organic forms to production-ready topology and UVs. This role is focused on creating complete, production-ready environment, vehicles, and prop models for our upcoming projects.

What You’ll Do:

  • Interpret 2D designs and translate them into 3D space while maintaining the original artistic intent. 
  • Produce complex or stylised environment models to a high standard with a strong understanding of appeal, silhouette, proportion, shape and scale.
  • Produce accurate UVs for models for use in downstream departments.

title: Final Layout Artist - Netflix Animation Studios

descriptionHtml:
Netflix Animation Studios is on a mission to entertain the world with bold, immersive animated films that are timeless and impactful. We are paving the way for the future of animation by building a community of amazing artists and talent across three vibrant locations globally. Come join us!

Job Summary:


We’re looking for versatile Final Layout Artists who have an eye for detail and a blend of creative and technical skills. Final Layout Artists help finalize set dressing, camera work, and shot assembly, ensuring that all components are ready for the final stages of production and that shots align with the film’s cinematic style and storytelling needs.


What You’ll Do:

  • Fine‑tune cinematic staging and camera positioning for assigned shots and sequences, as directed by the Final Layout Supervisor or Head of Cinematography, Layout
  • Work closely with Final Layout leadership to finalize camera setups—including framing, angles, movement, and focus—to enhance storytelling, performance, and visual impact
  • Refine and polish set dressing in shots, ensuring that all environment elements are visually cohesive and aligned with the Production Designer’s and Art Directors’ vision
  • Conform timing and casting of shots from previs/rough layout or editorial to match the latest edit, ensuring camera and asset usage align with the cut
  • Help maintain continuity and consistency of geography, scale, eye‑lines, and screen direction across shots and sequences
  • Set up and assemble final layout shots with all required assets and technical settings, ensuring scenes are cleanly structured and ready for Animation, CFX, FX, Lighting, and Compositing
  • Maintain and update shot breakdown information (e.g., asset usage, camera naming) and support QC of shots for downstream delivery
  • Work with layout tools and proprietary systems, and provide feedback on tools and workflows where appropriate
  • Collaborate with Animation, Environments, FX, CFX, Lighting, and Compositing teams to ensure final layout supports their needs and the wider production objectives
  • Communicate progress and potential challenges clearly to Supervisors and Production, and help troubleshoot creative and technical issues
  • Collaborate with grace, humility, inclusion, and open‑mindedness

What You’ll Need:

  • Previous experience as part of layout and/or previs teams on digital feature films, VFX projects, or high‑end series
  • Experience working within large digital feature film production pipelines
  • A reel or portfolio demonstrating strong camera work, shot composition, and layout/final layout skills
  • Working knowledge of previs/layout techniques, camera animation, and scene set‑up
  • Knowledge of cinematography and how to translate storyboards and animatics into 3D camera and shot design

The Stage Specialist is responsible for coordinating and supervising all activities on the stages to ensure seamless production operations. This role ensures that all stage resources, equipment, and logistics are efficiently managed to support the creative and technical needs of the production, while maintaining a safe and organized environment for cast, crew, and production vendors.  This is a demanding and fast moving position that requires someone who is a proactive and positive thinker, and able to exercise good judgment and communication.

The Production Finance team at Netflix is responsible for estimating and managing the production costs throughout the lifecycle of each production and provides insight and analytics to inform decision-making. The team understands the operations of a production and guides each project through its financial workflows required for a successful launch on the service.

We're looking for a Manager to join Netflix's Production Finance team in Indonesia, working closely with the Production Manager Lead and cross-functional partners across Creative, Physical Production, Post, VFX, and BALA. locations: Los Gatos, California, United States of America
descriptionHtml:
At Netflix, our mission is to entertain the world. Together, we are writing the next episode - pushing the boundaries of storytelling, global fandom and making the unimaginable a reality. We are a dream team obsessed with the uncomfortable excitement of discovering what happens when you merge creativity, intuition and cutting-edge technology. Come be a part of what’s next.


The Title and Launch Management (TLM) team is responsible for building and innovating the technology foundations that enable the ingest, setup, launch, and global distribution of all types of entertainment on Netflix—including series, movies, games, ads, live events, trailers, and more. TLM acts as the bridge between the title creation lifecycle and the consumer experience, ensuring that launching titles on Netflix is efficient, flexible, accurate, and scalable. Our team's goal is to make launching titles as seamless as possible, supporting both operational and creative needs across the company.


The Catalog Integration team turns the outputs of many independent content workflows into a coherent catalog that other systems can use. Partner teams create the artwork, language assets, ratings, descriptions, trailers, and other information that surrounds a title; Catalog Integration provides the federated data API and transformation layer that bring those outputs together, connects them into the catalog graph, and transforms them into a consistent view. 


We publish the real-time feeds that unblock every downstream, member-facing system — the moment our feeds go out, hundreds of services spring into action to serve that update to members. We invest in proprietary, cutting-edge tooling for data snapshots, recovery, graph-aware rollbacks, fast/override publication lanes, and realtime overrides, so that one bad entry never holds up the rest of the catalog. Our work enables Netflix's cutting edge business bets like Live, Games, and Sports while continuing to deliver the critical data that drives the streaming video content experience.


What you will do

You will lead a team of software engineers to deliver high-impact results. Your responsibilities in this role:


  • Own the reliability and timeliness of the real-time catalog feeds and publication pipeline that unblock every downstream, member-facing system, including the fast lanes and override lanes that keep a bad entry from holding up the rest of the catalog
  • Own Catalog Entity, our shared content modeling abstraction, evolving it to represent common structure and content-type-specific variation across films, episodic series, live shows, sports, and future content types without requiring a bespoke pipeline for each
  • Own the data integrity of the catalog: validate collected data against the model and business logic, hold back or override bad changes, and detect and remediate systemic feed failures
  • Partner with peer teams on setup-side object modeling and on the downstream member-facing contract
  • Lead collaboration with engineers, program managers, product managers, and other stakeholders to drive vision, strategy, and adoption
  • Foster a culture of accountability, ensuring timely and reliable delivery of the team's roadmap to support business needs
  • Act as a trusted technical advisor, guiding thoughtful decision-making in ambiguous situations
  • Communicate complex ideas clearly and influence decisions among diverse stakeholders
  • Balance business goals with strong engineering practices, investing in foundational work and continuous improvements
  • Hire, coach, and lead a team of engineers with deep data modeling and distributed systems expertise, inspiring exceptional results in stability, performance, and product experience
  • Build an inclusive team culture where everyone feels empowered, accepted, and respected

What we are looking for

  • 3 or more years building and managing high-performing, inclusive teams, attracting top talent, fostering accountability, and ensuring all voices inform decisions.
  • Experience delivering and operating high-performance data pipelines with near-real-time latency, balanced with consistency and partition tolerance, behind production internet consumer-scale workloads
  • Experience driving a culture of excellence, unlocking high-velocity business and product results while cultivating an ownership culture with best-in-breed systems reliability and operational readiness.
  • Proven ability to define and communicate systems strategy to drive long-term product feature enablement.
  • Skilled at prioritizing team efforts, aligning them with business objectives, and using data, input, and pilot investments to bring rigor to decision-making.
  • Effective communication and collaboration skills to build cross-functional partnerships, influence strategic direction, and empower team members across global teams.

Nice to have

  • Experience building generative AI solutions in ambiguous environments, with a proven ability to creatively experiment, develop innovative approaches, and collaborate effectively across cross-functional teams.
  • Experience leading engineering teams supporting large-scale data pipelines updating in the 10M+ updates/second regime
  • Experience with in-memory data snapshot architectures, point-in-time consistency, or graph-aware rollback/recovery systems
  • Experience leading the operation and optimization of CPU- and memory-intensive cloud services in the range of 1,000s to 10,000s of CPUss

title: Marketing Partnerships Creative Manager - Korea
locations: Seoul, Korea, Republic of
descriptionHtml:
Netflix is one of the world's leading entertainment services, with over 300 million paid memberships in over 190 countries enjoying TV series, films and games across a wide variety of genres and languages. Members can play, pause and resume watching as much as they want, anytime, anywhere, and can change their plans at any time.

It’s an exciting time to join Netflix as we continue to bring new stories to audiences around the world and expand how we work with brands and advertisers. Strategic partnerships and our advertising business create new opportunities to connect brands with entertainment, fandom, and engaged audiences.

Netflix works with brands and advertisers to create partnerships that bring our stories into culture in new ways. In Korea, the Marketing Partnerships Creative team leads the creative work behind these collaborations, connecting partner objectives, audience insights, and Netflix titles to develop campaigns that people want to engage with and talk about.

We’re looking for a Marketing Partnerships Creative Manager to lead this work from strategy through execution. The role spans two connected areas: consumer-facing campaigns created with brand partners and distribution partners, and B2B marketing and creative work that communicates the value of Netflix Ads to advertisers and agencies. This includes shaping compelling narratives, sales materials, and industry experiences that demonstrate how brands can connect with audiences through Netflix. Across both areas, you’ll translate business objectives into distinctive creative work grounded in a strong understanding of our brand, content, and audiences.


The role


You will work closely with Brand Partnerships / Partner Marketing Leads to identify opportunities, shape proposals, and lead the creative development of partnership campaigns. You’ll be involved from the earliest conversations: understanding a partner’s business challenge, finding a compelling role for Netflix and its titles, developing a strategic brief, and guiding the idea through production and launch.

You will be a partner-facing creative lead, working directly with advertisers and their agencies while bringing together teams across Netflix. You’ll lead briefings, workshops, presentations, and creative reviews; give clear direction and feedback; and ensure the final work delivers on its strategic intent, meets a high standard of creative excellence, and brings the Netflix brand and our titles to life in compelling ways.

You will also lead creative work that supports the Ads business, including pitch narratives, case studies, sales materials, and selected industry events and large-scale initiatives. This calls for someone who can move between big-picture thinking and hands-on delivery, managing multiple projects without losing sight of the idea.


Key responsibilities

  • Develop partnership opportunities and strategy. Explore Netflix titles and audiences to identify opportunities for partners. Connect partner objectives, consumer behavior, and cultural insights to create briefs, concepts, and presentations that can be pitched and developed into campaigns.
  • Lead campaigns end to end. Own creative strategy and development from the initial brief through ideation, planning, production, and execution. Ensure the campaign narrative remains clear and the work meets its business and creative objectives.
  • Lead the creative process with partners and agencies. Run workshops, briefings, presentations, and review sessions. Set direction, manage the feedback loop, and constructively challenge collaborators to make the work more distinctive and effective.
  • Oversee creative execution. Direct the development and delivery of campaign assets across relevant formats and channels. Manage creative and design agencies, vendors, and bespoke productions or shoots when needed.
  • Develop creative work for Ads marketing. Shape pitch narratives and lead the development of sales enablement materials, including presentations, video, print, social content, and case studies. Ensure the work communicates a compelling story, meets a high creative standard, and is reviewed, approved, and delivered on time.
  • Lead creative operations for major initiatives. Manage the creative workstream for selected Ads industry events and large-scale projects, including creative strategy and concepting, agency engagement, workflows, timelines, budgets, production, and coordination across teams.
  • Build alignment and protect the work. Partner closely with internal creative, marketing, sales, legal, and other relevant teams to navigate approvals and clearances. Ensure the Netflix brand and owned or licensed titles are represented and used appropriately throughout partner and Ads creative.

Qualifications and experience

  • 12+ years of experience in brand or consumer marketing, with substantial experience leading creative development at an advertising or integrated agency. In-house brand marketing / creative experience is a strong plus.
  • A proven ability to independently lead complex, integrated campaigns from brief and strategy through creative development, production, and launch.
  • Strong strategic thinking, with the ability to draw connections between business objectives, consumer research, behavior, culture, and content to find fertile ground for creative ideas.
  • Strong creative instincts and a media-agnostic approach. You can contribute ideas, shape and pitch concepts, write compelling briefs, and guide agencies toward work that feels fresh rather than expected.
  • Experience building trusted relationships with external partners and agencies, and aligning and influencing stakeholders across a complex, matrixed organization. You can navigate different organizational structures, dynamics, and working styles, adapting your communication with clarity, sound judgment, and diplomacy.
  • Solid production knowledge and project management skills. You can manage several workstreams, get into the details when needed, and solve problems while protecting the broader strategic intent.
  • Fluency in Korean and English, with the ability to communicate clearly and persuasively with internal teams and external senior stakeholders.
  • A deep understanding of the Korean market and the role cultural relevance plays in effective marketing. Experience in entertainment, content, or advertising partnerships is a plus.
  • Strong English proficiency; experience communicating and working with global teams and stakeholders is a plus.

How you work

You’re curious about entertainment and have a genuine interest in how people connect with stories, brands, and culture. You bring a point of view while staying open to other perspectives, and you know how to give and receive candid, constructive feedback.

You take ownership without needing a large team around you. You understand how to work across different organizations and working styles, communicate with judgment and diplomacy, and roll up your sleeves to move work forward when the path is unclear. You’re comfortable adapting as the business evolves and can thrive in Netflix’s culture of freedom and responsibility.

descriptionHtml:

We are a dream team obsessed with the uncomfortable excitement of discovering what happens when you merge creativity, intuition and cutting-edge technology. Come be a part of what’s next.

Netflix Games is looking for a Senior Portfolio Operations Manager to build the tools, data solutions, and rhythms that keep our games portfolio clear to the teams who support it. You'll design scalable tools and workflows, use AI to cut manual work and improve reporting, and lead the change management that lets the business adapt quickly.


Netflix Games is building the next generation of games for a worldwide audience. The Games portfolio sits where many teams across Netflix meet: Content, Marketing, Legal, Technology, Discovery, and more. Portfolio Operations Management is the connective tissue that keeps those teams in sync with what's happening across the portfolio.


We don't direct how games are made. We support the layer around them. We run shared portfolio tooling, keep portfolio state visible through reporting and monitoring, set and share the frameworks and standards that cross team boundaries, and help Games Leadership and cross-functional partners turn their needs into working processes.


The ideal candidate lives at the crossroads of program management and data solutions: equally comfortable leading a cross-functional program and designing the data model that powers it. You can effectively translate game production and development for non-production audiences, giving partners in Legal, Marketing, Finance, and Business Development the context they need to act. You'll develop, support, and improve the relational systems our partners rely on as their source of truth, find where AI and automation can remove friction, and deliver solutions that keep teams effortlessly connected. You're comfortable with ambiguity, you build trusting partnerships, and you prefer lightweight, scalable processes over heavy governance.


Responsibilities


  • Lead, scope, and operationalize cross-functional programs and projects involving multiple stakeholders with limited oversight.
  • Build and maintain scalable tools and workflows in our relational Airtable database: develop data models, build automations, and design interfaces.
  • Run regular audits to consolidate or retire redundant fields, tables, views, and automations, keeping systems performant, secure, and easy to navigate.
  • Use AI tools and agents for operational efficiency, workflow optimization, and intuitive reporting. Find high-leverage opportunities, prototype quickly, and bring proven solutions into production.
  • Improve portfolio reporting and data monitoring so Games Leadership and partners have accurate, timely visibility to ground and support their decisions.
  • Translate game production and development concepts (lifecycle phases, gates, milestones, live operations) into clear, actionable context for Games Leadership and non-production partners.
  • Own data hygiene and accuracy across the tools you support. Monitor health, fix what's broken, and help users serve themselves.
  • Turn a partner's need into a working process. Know when a tool, automation, playbook, workflow, report, or ritual is the right answer.
  • Own change management for rollouts, updates, and deprecations: testing, communication, training, adoption, and support - each grounded in a clear what, who, and why with confirmed buy-in.
  • Bring prioritized, evidence-backed feature requests and user stories to internal tooling and platform product and engineering owners on behalf of the portfolio.
  • Scope incoming work with discipline. Prioritize work that supports multiple users and that is backed by clear business objectives.
  • Write durable runbooks, training, and documentation so systems and rhythms outlast any one person.

Requirements


  • 8+ years in operations, program management, business systems, or a related field. Games experience preferred, but not required.
  • Hands-on experience designing and maintaining relational databases and the workflows built on them. Advanced Airtable experience (schema design, linked records, automations, scripting, interfaces) strongly preferred.
  • A track record of building scalable internal tools, automations, or reporting that other teams enthusiastically adopt and rely on.
  • Practical experience using AI tools (LLMs, agents, AI-assisted automation) to improve operations, workflows, or reporting, with good judgment about where AI adds value and where it doesn't.
  • Strong data skills: modeling, hygiene, and turning raw data into clear, decision-ready reporting. SQL, scripting (JavaScript or Python), or BI tool experience is a plus.
  • Knowledge of data governance principles, data quality standards, and metadata management.
  • Proven change management skills, landing rollouts across many stakeholders with measurable adoption.
  • Ability to translate stakeholder needs into clear requirements and user stories for product and engineering teams.
  • Clear, proactive communicator who builds lasting partnerships across leadership, production, development, and highly matrixed cross-functional teams.
  • Comfortable with ambiguity, with a people-over-process mindset and a bias toward lightweight, adoptable solutions.

title: Staff Software Engineer 6  - Java Platform Team
locations: Warsaw, Poland
descriptionHtml:
Netflix is one of the world's leading entertainment services, with over 300 million paid memberships in over 190 countries enjoying TV series, films and games across a wide variety of genres and languages. Members can play, pause and resume watching as much as they want, anytime, anywhere, and can change their plans at any time.

The Mission


The Java Platform Team is moving from "best effort" support to a fully managed, curated "Paved Path" (our recommended, supported standard path) for Java at Netflix. Our Spring Boot based application framework is the most ergonomic choice for most Java development and remains at the center of that path. Some workloads, such as sidecars, and lightweight containers, batch/stream processing jobs, have tight limits on memory and startup time, and they still need the same Netflix platform capabilities.

We make Spring Boot work well in a sidecar or lightweight container, with a leaner footprint and faster startup. We also create standalone, constructible Java libraries that give any Java process access to Netflix platform primitives such as configuration, observability, discovery, and networking. The same libraries work inside our Spring Boot framework and outside it, so there is one source of truth and updates reach every consumer.


The Role


As a Staff Engineer you set technical direction for this area of the Java Platform Team. You own the architecture of the library set, decide what belongs in it and what does not, and raise the bar for the engineers around you. You are hands-on in code and design, and you make the hard calls on API shape, compatibility, and scope.

You will:

  • Define the architecture of our lightweight library set. Design builder and constructor based APIs for core platform primitives. Decide how each component runs standalone, inside Spring Boot applications, and in a sidecar or light container, without duplicating logic across those modes.
  • Fully support sidecars and light containers. Make Spring Boot applications run well in these environments, for example through minimal starters and trimmed runtimes. Set and defend footprint and startup budgets (small memory, fast startup, small disk footprint). Build benchmarking and regression checks that maintain those budgets across releases. Design the integration and regression testing that lets library changes reach consumers with high confidence and minimal disruption.
  • Own interface stability. We commit to long-term support for anything we ship to GA. You set the versioning, compatibility, and side-by-side version strategy, and own the migration cost of any breaking change.
  • Work closely with the wider Java Platform Team and partner teams. Make sure our lightweight libraries and the Spring Boot framework share the same underlying components, and help that framework become a better fit for more use cases, for example through minimal starters. Align with Compute, Service Mesh, and other platform teams on gRPC, metrics, and configuration standards for the polyglot Netflix ecosystem.
  • Guide customers to the right path with focus on developer experience. Work with engineering teams and product managers to understand their needs, decide whether the answer is the Spring Boot framework, the lightweight libraries, or better guidance, and help them adopt it. Look for underserved use cases and work with customers to understand them.
  • Lead through others. Mentor engineers, review designs, and write the memos and decision records that set direction. Help build the Warsaw hub into a team that owns its area independently.

Who You Are


  • Staff-level experience designing and owning shared libraries or platform components used by many teams, including managing the long-term impact of API decisions. Demonstrated experience in Java and distributed systems, with emphasis on scope, complexity, and impact.
  • A technical leader without needing authority. You have led multi-team technical efforts, resolved disagreement between strong engineers, and made hard-to-reverse decisions with incomplete information. You write things down so others can challenge them.
  • An end-to-end owner. You take a problem from discovery through design, rollout, telemetry, and iteration, and you measure whether it worked.
  • User focused. You learn what teams need before deciding what to build.
  • An invested mentor and coach. You support the growth of other engineers through mentoring, knowledge sharing, and feedback.

Core Competencies


  • Modern Java expertise (Java 17 and 21 or later). Standard library, concurrency, and especially API design for long-lived public interfaces.
  • JVM internals and performance. Memory model, garbage collection tuning, class loading, startup time, and footprint in constrained environments. You profile before you optimize.
  • Library and dependency design. Minimal dependency trees, classpath isolation, binary compatibility, and how to ship a library that works across different runtimes and containers.
  • Distributed systems fundamentals. gRPC, HTTP, service mesh, metrics and configuration systems, and their failure modes.
  • Automation mindset. You build developer tooling (testing frameworks, compatibility checks, linters, CLIs) that removes toil for other engineers.
  • Empathy and inclusivity. You value candor, seek out different perspectives, and build tools that work for every engineer, not just experts.

Nice to Have


  • Familiarity with Spring internals, enough to integrate cleanly with Spring Boot applications.
  • Experience with JVM startup and footprint techniques (for example class data sharing, jlink, or ahead-of-time compilation) and knowing when they are worth their cost.
  • Experience building or operating sidecars, agents, or containerized Java services with tight resource limits.
  • Experience with Gradle plugin development or build tooling.

A Typical Challenge


"How do we give a sidecar, a batch job, and a Spring service the same configuration and metrics library, keep its interface stable for years, and stay within a tight memory budget?"


You Might Be a Good Fit If


  • You want to define the interface that hundreds of engineers build on, rather than build a single product feature.
  • You build concise, versatile, and scalable libraries that solve real customer problems, and you can explain your design choices.
  • You can make, explain, and revise architectural decisions in writing.
  • You care about footprint and startup time as much as features.

Not Ticking Every Box?


At Netflix, we value talent, passion, and the ability to learn over a perfect checklist. If you can see yourself contributing to a stable, minimal, and fast Java paved path that works with Spring and beyond it, we want to hear from you.

descriptionHtml:
Netflix Animation Studios is on a mission to entertain the world with bold, immersive animated films that are timeless and impactful. We are paving the way for the future of animation by building a community of amazing artists and talent across three vibrant locations globally. Come join us!

Job Summary


We are seeking a Rigging Supervisor to support our upcoming feature film. The Rigging Supervisor works inside of NAS to lead the rigging team on a specific film or series, overseeing the creation and maintenance of high-quality rigs for characters, creatures, props, and vehicles.


This role ensures that rigs are animator‑friendly, technically robust, and well integrated into the studio pipeline, working within the direction and standards set by the Head of Characters, Head of Assets, and show Technical Supervisor.


What You’ll Do


  • Supervise the development of rigs for characters, creatures, props, and vehicles that support the show’s animation style and performance goals.
  • Collaborate with Animation, Modeling, CFX, and Crowd leadership to understand requirements and ensure rigs enable expressive, efficient, and reliable motion.

  • Work with Technical Supervisors, Asset TDs, and Production Technology to help define and refine rigging workflows, tools, validators, and naming standards.

title: Language Producer, Content Localisation - India
locations: Mumbai, India
descriptionHtml:
Netflix is one of the world's leading entertainment services, with over 300 million paid memberships in over 190 countries enjoying TV series, films and games across a wide variety of genres and languages. Members can play, pause and resume watching as much as they want, anytime, anywhere, and can change their plans at any time.

As a Language Producer, you will ensure that members experience the highest quality localized assets, preserving creative intent and enhancing the localized experience for viewers everywhere. With Netflix's global reach and ever-evolving entertainment footprint, world-class localization support for new languages and content genres is essential to our success, making this an exciting time to join the company.


The Role

The Language Producer is the advocate for language quality, creative consistency, and cultural authenticity across all localized Netflix content in their assigned language(s). This role oversees the end-to-end creative and linguistic aspects of dubbing, subtitling, main/episodic titles, accessibility, and marketing assets, serving as the key point of contact for all language-specific localization efforts. Approximately 40% of the role is dedicated to direct title and project coverage—supporting long-form project progress, creative strategy and quality control, and the launch of all localized assets—while the remaining 60% focuses on strategic market and talent development, including workflow innovation, vendor management, and building a robust talent pipeline. This is in support and collaboration with Content Localization Title Producers.  The Language Producer partners with internal teams and external talent to deliver high-quality, culturally relevant content. By monitoring language trends and maintaining deep market awareness, this role ensures every Netflix story resonates authentically with local audiences and upholds the highest standards of creative excellence.


Key Responsibilities


Language Quality & Creative Excellence
  • Establish and enforce creative and quality standards and guidelines for all localized content in your assigned language(s), ensuring consistency across dubbing, subtitling, main/episodic titles, accessibility, and marketing assets.
  • Develop, implement, and maintain language strategies that prioritize localization efforts based on business impact and creative requirements.
  • Monitor language performance metrics and emerging linguistic trends, proactively identifying and resolving quality or consistency challenges.

Cross-Functional Collaboration & Advocacy
  • Partner closely with Content Localization Title Producers, Product Localization, Marketing, and other cross-functional teams to align on localization strategy, execution, and creative direction for your language(s).
  • Represent language-specific needs and perspectives in cross-team initiatives, integration projects, and support for emerging media types.
  • Ensure robust communication channels between local language teams and global stakeholders, advocating for both local nuance and global consistency.

Vendor & Resource Management
  • Inform the consolidation and strategic assignment of vendors at the language level to maximize efficiency, quality, and scalability.
  • Collaborate with Global Resource Management to evaluate, refine, and implement vendor strategies and resource allocation for your language(s).
  • Oversee the selection, onboarding, and ongoing management of language-specific resources, ensuring a strong, reliable talent pipeline.

Talent & Market Engagement
  • Build and maintain strong relationships with local dubbing and subtitling talent, studios, and industry communities to support creative excellence and market relevance.
  • Maintain and regularly update a robust database of language talent in partnership with vendors, performance and specialization.
  • Monitor union, guild, and competitor activity to anticipate market shifts, inform strategy, and maintain a competitive edge in talent engagement.

Innovation, Change & Scalability
  • Serve as the local Subject Matter Expert (SME) in Netflix tooling and workflows, providing guidance to vendors on effective adoption, troubleshooting, and best practices to ensure seamless integration and operational excellence.
  • Champion the adoption of new workflows, automation, and technology to streamline localization processes and support the localization of emerging media types (e.g., interactive, live, podcasts).
  • Lead initiatives to enhance quality at scale, expedite project timelines, and ensure business continuity across all content types and workflows.
  • Foster a culture of continuous improvement, encouraging experimentation and the sharing of best practices within the local industry.

Inclusion & Diversity
  • Lead and support initiatives to ensure inclusive and diverse engagement of language talent and resources.
  • Ensure that localization strategies and talent pipelines reflect both the nuances of local audiences and the broader goals of global consistency and representation.
  • Champion global diversity, equity, and inclusion efforts in language production.

Requirements

  • 5 or more years of experience in content localization, dubbing, subtitle, or international versioning for premium TV/film services
  • Fluency in English required; fluency in local market language required.  Additional languages are a plus.
  • Deep expertise in both dubbing and subtitling workflows, with a strong passion for language quality and cultural nuance.
  • Ability to handle a fast-paced environment, supervising several projects at various points of production (from development through delivery).
  • Linguistic expertise and previous localization experience in your local market language(s).
  • Deep understanding of localization workflows, tools, and best practices, with a track record of delivering high-quality language assets at scale.
  • Excellent communication and relationship-building skills; able to work effectively in collaboration with creative, operational, and technical teams.
  • Make sound independent decisions, and know when to escalate issues.
  • Highly analytical, data-driven, and solutions-oriented; able to identify root causes, optimize processes, and drive operational excellence.
  • Adaptable and resilient in the face of change and ambiguity; comfortable with evolving priorities and new challenges.
  • Passion for creative storytelling, regional authenticity, and delivering an exceptional member experience.
  • Experience with accessibility standards (SDH, Audio Description) and emerging media formats is a plus.
  • Willingness to travel as needed.

descriptionHtml:

Role & Responsibilities


Partner Operations is obsessed with making direct delivery simpler for new content partners and the Netflix teams who receive and launch their titles day-to-day. We evaluate what the partner can deliver, how those assets might move through fulfillment and launch systems, and what it takes to support the deal day to day.


As a Partner Operations Manager, you will be the operational lead across an assigned slate of deals. You will assess what a partner can deliver, decide the appropriate delivery path, guide the partner through first deliveries and set up a process that Operations teams can run day to day. You will balance the partner experience with the work required of Netflix teams and vendors, and make the important decisions and handoffs clear.


In this role, you will:

  • Clarify deal goals, asset and localization needs, timing, partner contacts and open questions with Business Development, Regional Merchandising and Content teams as deals move into delivery planning.
  • Assess the partner’s ability to meet our specs. Compare their needs with Netflix’s current system and operational capabilities; identify what is missing, what may need to be built and the effort required from integration through stable operations.
  • Apply gateway eligibility criteria agreed with Engineering to determine delivery through UI, API or a vendor route. Work with Ops Vendor Management on the vendor model and cost, considering the effort for the partner and Netflix teams.
  • Lead pre-qualification across long-form and promotional assets. Coordinate sample and quality reviews, then determine which assets Netflix can accept or conform, what the partner must change and whether vendor or post-vendor QC is needed.
  • Turn partner context and deal nuance into clear technical and operational requirements for Product and Engineering. Frame the problem, define the workflow and write user stories where useful, making timing, constraints and trade-offs clear. Work with PACT and Solution Engineering on configuration and integration questions.
  • Prepare partners to meet spec, coordinate tests and work through first deliveries. Answer delivery and spec questions clearly, bring in technical specialists when needed and remove early blockers.
  • Keep partners, vendors and internal teams aligned on decisions, risks, owners and next steps. Communicate early and on time, and anticipate what each team will need before it becomes a problem.
  • Hand off the partner profile, setup and open risks to the Launch Ops project manager once delivery is reliable.

Requirements:

  • Substantial experience independently leading complex partner onboarding, post-production, content operations, or product launches. This is a role for someone who has taken ambiguous, multi-team work from planning through launch and stable operations.
  • Proven project or technical program management experience, with strong judgment on priorities, dependencies, risk and when to escalate.
  • Excellent partner management. You build trust, set expectations, navigate difficult conversations and stay several steps ahead of partners and internal teams.
  • Clear, timely written and verbal communication. You can explain technical and operational issues in plain language and turn them into decisions, owners and next steps. 
  • Strong experience coordinating Product, Engineering, Operations, business teams and external vendors toward a common launch outcome.
  • Confidence working directly with Product and Engineering. You can turn partner context into clear problem statements, workflow requirements and user stories; discuss APIs and configurations; and understand engineering roadmap priorities and trade-offs.
  • An understanding of the Netflix product or comparable streaming products, the content delivery and fulfillment ecosystem, and how delivery choices affect the member experience. Familiarity with media specifications, media processing, QC and direct delivery tools is helpful.
  • The ability to move comfortably between detail and the end-to-end picture, making the partner experience simpler while keeping ongoing operational work sustainable.
